comment: Plain-English headlines + summaries per motion, generated by `python -m ingest.summarize_motions` and merged into docs/data*.json by build_dataset. Keyed by a content hash of the motion (see summarize_motions.motion_key) — NOT by motion id, which renumbers. Safe to hand-edit: a corrected entry is never overwritten unless you pass --force.

001ec9fe12aed779.headline: Routine items grouped; two land items pulled out
001ec9fe12aed779.summary: The council took up its batch of routine consent items, pulling the two Overland land agreements out to be handled separately.
001ec9fe12aed779.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the housekeeping step that clears routine items in one vote and moves the two land items into open discussion.

00f4aee32d7d1f3c.headline: Land moved from Cedar Fort into Eagle Mountain
00f4aee32d7d1f3c.summary: The council moved a piece of property out of the Town of Cedar Fort and into Eagle Mountain's city boundaries.
00f4aee32d7d1f3c.impact: If you own or live on that land, Eagle Mountain now provides your city services and sets your taxes and zoning rules instead of Cedar Fort. The motion doesn't identify the property.

010cc8116542304e.headline: Charlotte Ducos joins Community Services Board
010cc8116542304e.summary: The council appointed Charlotte Ducos to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, from April 2026 through March 2028.
010cc8116542304e.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer appointment to an advisory board.

024c282a213d4f6c.headline: Karan Heffelfinger joins Senior Citizens Advisory Council
024c282a213d4f6c.summary: Karan Heffelfinger was appointed to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council for a four-year term running through December 2027.
024c282a213d4f6c.impact: Routine appointment — nothing changes for residents.

03102490b6f271b6.headline: Debra Kimbrough joins the Senior Advisory Board
03102490b6f271b6.summary: The council appointed Debra Kimbrough to a three-year term on the Senior Advisory Board, from April 2026 through March 2029.
03102490b6f271b6.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a volunteer seat on a board that advises the council rather than making decisions.

0355882506985103.headline: Third vote on the new school district agreement
0355882506985103.summary: The council approved the same school district agreement with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield Town a third time, recorded under yet another resolution number.
0355882506985103.impact: Nothing new here for you — it's the same agreement as the previous motion, logged under a different resolution number.

045508bfe3480d39.headline: Casitas and garage apartments allowed, with parking rule
045508bfe3480d39.summary: The city set rules for backyard and in-home rentals, allowing casitas, guest houses and apartments over a detached garage, and requiring two off-street parking spaces.
045508bfe3480d39.impact: If you want to add a casita, guest house, or apartment over your garage, the rules now clearly allow it — but you will have to provide off-street parking for two vehicles.

049228c18a1c7172.headline: QTS development agreement amended
049228c18a1c7172.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's development agreement with QTS; the motion doesn't say what the amendment changes.
049228c18a1c7172.impact: A development agreement sets what a company may build and what it owes the city, so changes here can matter. The record doesn't say what was changed.

04ffe30331fff727.headline: New rules for second kitchens in homes
04ffe30331fff727.summary: The city added a new section to its code, Chapter 17.69, setting rules for second kitchens and kitchenettes in homes.
04ffe30331fff727.impact: If you have or are planning a second kitchen in your house, it is now regulated by the city. The motion itself doesn't spell out the requirements, so check with the planning department before building one.

05791ef29bb484c7.headline: Public comment set on new school district
05791ef29bb484c7.summary: The council formally accepted a feasibility study on creating a new school district and scheduled public comment for June 13 and June 18, 2024, ahead of a final decision.
05791ef29bb484c7.impact: If you have kids in school or pay property taxes here, those two dates are your chance to weigh in before the council decides whether to create the district.

05b2b8cf12484072.headline: City backs moving the rodeo grounds
05b2b8cf12484072.summary: The council declared its intent to work with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape committee on relocating the city rodeo grounds into the buffer area around Camp Williams.
05b2b8cf12484072.impact: Nothing moves yet — this only commits the city to work with the partner group on a possible new site. If you use the rodeo grounds, expect a relocation plan to come back for a real decision later.

05b7a0e34797dda9.headline: Gas power plant approved on Pony Express Parkway
05b7a0e34797dda9.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Will-Power UT for a natural gas power plant, limited to simple-cycle technology and required to be running within five years.
05b7a0e34797dda9.impact: A gas-fired power plant is now cleared to be built, with trees required along Pony Express Parkway. If you live nearby, expect construction within the next five years unless the company gets an extension.

05e56835da36deb9.headline: Design rules for shops and apartments put on hold
05e56835da36deb9.summary: The council delayed a decision on updated design standards for commercial and apartment buildings, sending them back for final changes before another vote.
05e56835da36deb9.impact: Nothing changes yet. The rules that govern what new stores and apartment buildings must look like stay as they are until the council takes the item up again.

07480df28e49ae05.headline: Justice court with Utah County added to priorities
07480df28e49ae05.summary: The council added pursuing a justice court with Utah County to its Legislative Priorities List.
07480df28e49ae05.impact: Nothing changes now, and no court is being created. This only flags the idea as something the city intends to pursue.

07aab5d2e036d00d.headline: Council must be told when concept plans go forward
07aab5d2e036d00d.summary: The city changed its development rules so the council is notified every time a concept plan is set to go before the Planning Commission.
07aab5d2e036d00d.impact: Nothing changes day to day for residents. Council members simply get advance notice of proposed developments before the Planning Commission reviews them.

07e05b70e32db99f.headline: Consent agenda approved
07e05b70e32db99f.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of routine items passed together in a single vote; the record does not list which items it contained.
07e05b70e32db99f.impact: Nothing here for residents — consent agendas are routine housekeeping like meeting minutes and standard renewals.

088cec0df8eae363.headline: Join the Utah Valley HOME Consortium
088cec0df8eae363.summary: The city agreed to sign a cooperation agreement joining the Utah Valley HOME Consortium alongside other participating local governments.
088cec0df8eae363.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day — this is the paperwork that formally enrolls Eagle Mountain in a regional partnership with neighboring governments.

08965103f564aace.headline: Consent agenda and new city recorder approved
08965103f564aace.summary: The council passed its consent agenda, including changes to the year's financial audit discussed in work session, and appointed Gina Olsen as city recorder.
08965103f564aace.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this is the batch of routine items the council passes together, plus the staff appointment that keeps the city's official records.

08e94283a45399db.headline: Building and construction rules updated
08e94283a45399db.summary: The council changed the city's building and construction rules in Title 15 of the municipal code; the record does not spell out what changed.
08e94283a45399db.impact: If you are building or remodeling, the rules you have to follow have shifted — though the meeting record does not say how. Most residents will notice nothing.

096d839c99c68bdf.headline: Development agreement with Flagship Homes approved
096d839c99c68bdf.summary: The city approved a development agreement with homebuilder Flagship Homes; the motion itself names no location, acreage, or number of homes.
096d839c99c68bdf.impact: A development agreement locks in the terms a builder must follow before it breaks ground. The motion doesn't say where this project sits or how many homes it covers, so the effect on any one neighborhood is unclear.

0a02f1c779cb9430.headline: Triple Tail redevelopment plan adopted
0a02f1c779cb9430.summary: The city adopted the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, covering 24 parcels, to steer that land toward new development and economic uses.
0a02f1c779cb9430.impact: If you live near 4000 North and Pole Canyon Boulevard east of Tyson Parkway, or south of 1000 North east of Pony Express Parkway, expect the city to actively pursue development on the land around you.

0bb5dad0d7a7d643.headline: Outdoor watering banned in part of the city
0bb5dad0d7a7d643.summary: The city put a short-term ban on outdoor water use in one area of Eagle Mountain, still allowing water for animals, hand-watered gardens, and drip irrigation.
0bb5dad0d7a7d643.impact: If you live in the affected area, you cannot water your lawn or use water outdoors until the ban lifts. You can still water animals, hand-water a garden, and run drip irrigation. The rest of the city is unaffected.

0c147e143b656d14.headline: Eagle Square shopping center plat delayed
0c147e143b656d14.summary: The council delayed a decision on the Eagle Square commercial preliminary plat until legal wording in the related development agreement is sorted out.
0c147e143b656d14.impact: Work on this commercial project cannot move forward until the council takes it up again. Nothing changes for residents in the meantime.

0c5f723addeb7f5c.headline: Moderate income housing plan updated
0c5f723addeb7f5c.summary: The council amended the moderate income housing section of the city's General Plan, the long-range document that guides future housing decisions.
0c5f723addeb7f5c.impact: Nothing changes for you right away. The motion doesn't say which housing policies were changed, only that the long-range plan was amended.

0cd454b6f97c2306.headline: Adelle Curtis appointed to the Library Board
0cd454b6f97c2306.summary: Adelle Curtis was appointed to the Library Board for a two-year term running through December 2025.
0cd454b6f97c2306.impact: Routine appointment — nothing changes for residents. She is one of the people who will advise the city on the library.

0db6f7e97ac84b03.headline: Consent agenda approved, four items pulled
0db6f7e97ac84b03.summary: The council approved its consent agenda while pushing two sets of minutes to a later meeting and moving two other items to full discussion.
0db6f7e97ac84b03.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this only decides which items get talked through and which wait for a future meeting.

0e288f8eb26a6482.headline: Changes to street-connection and site plan rules
0e288f8eb26a6482.summary: The council amended the code sections that govern how new developments connect to surrounding streets and how site plans are reviewed.
0e288f8eb26a6482.impact: Nothing changes for existing homes. These standards apply to builders laying out new subdivisions and commercial sites; the motion itself does not spell out what the revised language says.

0e5c9773fb602a5b.headline: Land-sale policy added to council's priority list
0e5c9773fb602a5b.summary: The council put writing a policy for how staff review applications to buy city-owned land onto its list of legislative priorities.
0e5c9773fb602a5b.impact: Nothing changes right now — this only commits the city to drafting rules later for how it handles requests to buy public land.

0e99c5b5d094e625.headline: City to dispose of 2.15 acres of land
0e99c5b5d094e625.summary: The council approved disposing of 2.15 acres of city-owned land at Utah County parcel 59:044:0015 and set the terms.
0e99c5b5d094e625.impact: This land leaves city hands. The motion does not say who receives it or what will go there, so there is nothing concrete yet for neighbors to plan around.

0f4b0b622fb14d15.headline: Wendy's approved on Pony Express Parkway
0f4b0b622fb14d15.summary: The city approved the site plan for a Wendy's at 4302 Pony Express Parkway, adding conditions on trees, crosswalk lighting, and building lighting.
0f4b0b622fb14d15.impact: A new Wendy's is coming to that stretch of Pony Express Parkway in The Ranches. The site's crosswalk has to be lit brightly enough to meet the city's safety code before it opens.

0f5f22581bcf6ce2.headline: Tax deal set up for Sweetwater #4 project area
0f5f22581bcf6ce2.summary: The city and its redevelopment agency signed an agreement spelling out how property tax growth from the Sweetwater #4 project area gets collected and passed along.
0f5f22581bcf6ce2.impact: Nothing changes on your tax bill. This is the paperwork that routes future tax growth from that one area to the redevelopment agency so the project plan can work.

0f65e7bcb0db82ab.headline: Steve Conger joins the Community Services Board
0f65e7bcb0db82ab.summary: The council appointed Steve Conger to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, from April 2026 through March 2029.
0f65e7bcb0db82ab.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer appointment to an advisory board.

1085e33ad2393a03.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook rezoning put on hold
1085e33ad2393a03.summary: The council delayed a decision on rezoning the land known as Cedar Valley Holbrook.
1085e33ad2393a03.impact: Nothing changes for now. The proposal is set aside and has to come back to the council before anything about that land is decided.

10ccef440f602d9d.headline: Consent agenda approved, four items pulled
10ccef440f602d9d.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling four items out of it for separate discussion.
10ccef440f602d9d.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. The four pulled items were taken up individually later in the meeting.

10f1acd70c87dc7a.headline: Outside brokers allowed for big city land deals
10f1acd70c87dc7a.summary: The city authorized staff to hire a real estate brokerage or a real estate attorney when buying or selling major city property.
10f1acd70c87dc7a.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this only sets who the city can bring in to handle its larger land purchases and sales.

1157520139222e49.headline: Bryan Free joins the planning commission
1157520139222e49.summary: The council signed off on appointing Bryan Free to the planning commission for a one-year term through December 2026.
1157520139222e49.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day. The planning commission reviews building and zoning proposals before they reach the council, so who sits on it shapes what gets built.

11c6491142ddab9b.headline: Second vote on the new school district agreement
11c6491142ddab9b.summary: The council approved the same April 29 agreement with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield Town to create a new school district, under a different resolution number.
11c6491142ddab9b.impact: Nothing new here for you — it's the same agreement as the previous motion, logged under a different resolution number.

12bc3ca6fe380d6f.headline: Consent agenda passed, one fee raised to $2,000
12bc3ca6fe380d6f.summary: The council approved its bundle of routine items after pulling three out for separate debate, and raised one fee from $250 to $2,000.
12bc3ca6fe380d6f.impact: Whoever pays that fee will now owe $2,000 instead of $250, and one purchase agreement had to be signed by May 27. The motion doesn't say what the fee covers, so most residents will see no change.

132335f0906ee7ed.headline: Consent agenda approved
132335f0906ee7ed.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items voted through together without separate discussion.
132335f0906ee7ed.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the routine batch vote the council uses to clear uncontested items in one step.

13b4b87f46d5ada3.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 rezoning put off
13b4b87f46d5ada3.summary: The council delayed a decision on rezoning the land known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 and left its public hearing open.
13b4b87f46d5ada3.impact: If you live near Cedar Corners, nothing changes yet — the current zoning stays, and you will still be able to speak when the hearing resumes.

141ef92eb43cc5b4.headline: Decision delayed on Towns at Brylee Farms
141ef92eb43cc5b4.summary: The council delayed a decision on the development agreement for the Towns at Brylee Farms project.
141ef92eb43cc5b4.impact: Nothing changes for now — the project is on hold until the council takes it up again.

141fb27cfde742d2.headline: Fence and screening rules changed
141fb27cfde742d2.summary: The city changed the part of its code that governs fences and screening, though the motion does not spell out the new provisions.
141fb27cfde742d2.impact: If you are putting up a fence or screening on your property anywhere in the city, check the current code before you build — the rules that apply to you have changed.

1437e36981270e98.headline: Consent agenda approved
1437e36981270e98.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the bundle of items passed together in one vote; the record does not list what was in it.
1437e36981270e98.impact: Nothing in the record points to a specific change for residents, because the items grouped into this single vote were not listed.

14bfd952effb0b0c.headline: Consent agenda approved
14bfd952effb0b0c.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling one item out for separate discussion and changing another item's effective date to the date of closing.
14bfd952effb0b0c.impact: This is routine housekeeping — the batch of items the council passes without separate debate. Nothing here changes for residents on its own.

14dea4e84b22e24e.headline: New parking and screening rules citywide
14dea4e84b22e24e.summary: The city rewrote its parking and landscaping rules, requiring screening plants at least 3.5 feet tall when planted and vegetation that screens year-round.
14dea4e84b22e24e.impact: This mostly affects builders and businesses planning new lots. Where a project sits next to homes, screening plants must already be 3.5 feet tall and stay green through the winter.

1546234f3d654fa7.headline: Susan Allen appointed as senior citizen advisor
1546234f3d654fa7.summary: The council appointed Susan Allen as a Senior Citizen Advisor, serving through December 31, 2025.
1546234f3d654fa7.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this fills a volunteer advisory seat through the end of the year.

162d6b9af76b57b2.headline: "Newspaper" update to subdivision and zoning code
162d6b9af76b57b2.summary: The council amended two chapters of city code — 16.05 on subdivisions and 17.05 on zoning — in what the city calls the Newspaper Amendment.
162d6b9af76b57b2.impact: The motion does not say what the amendment actually changes, so there is nothing concrete residents will see or do differently based on this text alone.

17abba79553f22e5.headline: $190K more for the Firefly water tank
17abba79553f22e5.summary: The council took up a change order adding $189,985.67 to the cost of the Firefly 4-million-gallon water tank.
17abba79553f22e5.impact: This adds money to a city water storage tank already under contract. The motion sets no change to your water bill, and the record does not show a final outcome.

17e40cd736dfd527.headline: Meeting recessed at 10:57 p.m.
17e40cd736dfd527.summary: The council recessed its March 6 meeting at 10:57 p.m.
17e40cd736dfd527.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents.

18b41a4ed883bdf2.headline: Sign height now measured from natural grade
18b41a4ed883bdf2.summary: The city changed its sign rules so a sign's height is measured from the natural ground level rather than an altered one.
18b41a4ed883bdf2.impact: If you are putting up a sign — mostly businesses and developers — the allowed height is now measured from the original ground, so building up the dirt underneath will not buy extra height.

198d0d9c3de06305.headline: Five city boards folded into one
198d0d9c3de06305.summary: The council took up an ordinance replacing five volunteer boards — parks and recreation, sports, cemetery, veterans, and economic development — with a single Community Services Board.
198d0d9c3de06305.impact: If you serve on one of these boards or bring issues to them, they would be consolidated into one Community Services Board. For everyone else, nothing changes day to day.

19946c45c2fadb30.headline: School land transfer tied to replacing school site
19946c45c2fadb30.summary: The city agreed to a property transfer inside the new west county school district, on the condition that a replacement parcel is bought for the elementary school.
19946c45c2fadb30.impact: This matters to families waiting on the elementary school: the city's consent only holds if the district buys replacement land, so a site has to stay set aside for the school.

19e990beeef1819f.headline: Expired development deals now trigger rezoning
19e990beeef1819f.summary: The council required the planning director to start rezoning land whenever a master development agreement or development agreement on it expires or is terminated.
19e990beeef1819f.impact: If you own land covered by a development agreement that lapses, the city will move to rezone it rather than leave the old zoning in place. Most residents will not notice this.

19fdd9af77c0844d.headline: Amenity swap rules added to code to-do list
19fdd9af77c0844d.summary: The council put a future code change on its legislative priorities list requiring developers to request amenity exchanges early in the approval process.
19fdd9af77c0844d.impact: Nothing changes yet — this only adds the rule to the city's list of code updates to write later. If it is eventually adopted, developers swapping promised neighborhood amenities would have to ask sooner.

1aeb19e33a0fd005.headline: Zoning set for Eagle Mountain Properties parcels
1aeb19e33a0fd005.summary: The council took up a zoning change covering 27 parcels in the Eagle Mountain Properties master plan area, setting most to agriculture with several neighborhood commercial and two low-density residential.
1aeb19e33a0fd005.impact: Zoning decides what can be built on those parcels. Nothing changes for existing homes today, but it shapes what neighbors could see built on that land later.

1afc21853f708a71.headline: Pay schedule set for elected city officers
1afc21853f708a71.summary: The council added a new chapter to city code setting the compensation schedule for Eagle Mountain's statutory officers.
1afc21853f708a71.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this puts officer pay into the city code. The motion lists no salary figures.

1bcd71f6b39c0618.headline: Final zoning set for the White Hills area
1bcd71f6b39c0618.summary: The council assigned final zoning across the White Hills area, including one commercial lot, two agricultural parcels, and ten parcels set to rural agriculture.
1bcd71f6b39c0618.impact: If you own land in White Hills, this fixes what you may build there — most of it stays rural or farm land, with one parcel opened to neighborhood-scale commercial use.

1bd3b8d56f5dd862.headline: Zoning definitions updated
1bd3b8d56f5dd862.summary: The council updated the definitions section of the city's land use code; the motion does not say which terms were changed.
1bd3b8d56f5dd862.impact: Nothing changes day to day. Definitions set the meaning of terms used elsewhere in the zoning code, and matter mainly to developers and the staff applying those rules.

1c188b116578f003.headline: Decision delayed on SITLA land swap in Overland
1c188b116578f003.summary: The council delayed a decision on a land exchange agreement with the state land trust, SITLA, for properties in the Overland area.
1c188b116578f003.impact: No land changed hands and nothing changes for residents right now — the swap comes back to the council at a later meeting.

1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.headline: Sewer master plan and impact fee plan approved
1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.summary: The council approved the city's wastewater master plan and the impact fee facilities plan setting out which sewer projects new growth is expected to pay for.
1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.impact: Sewer service at existing homes doesn't change. The plan is the basis the city uses to charge impact fees on new construction, so it mainly touches builders and anyone building a new home here.

1caeedf39d59002d.headline: $20,000 added for a special-events UTV
1caeedf39d59002d.summary: The city added $20,000 to the special events budget line so staff have more flexibility in choosing a utility task vehicle.
1caeedf39d59002d.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this is a budget adjustment that lets the events crew pick a different utility vehicle than the one first budgeted for.

1dc55f3b8940cb04.headline: Consent agenda approved
1dc55f3b8940cb04.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together in a single vote without separate discussion.
1dc55f3b8940cb04.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the routine step that clears grouped housekeeping items in one go.

1e54ecf0681505b1.headline: Council rules rewrite delayed to February
1e54ecf0681505b1.summary: The council put off an ordinance spelling out the powers of the mayor, council and staff, sending it back to the city attorney for rewording before February 6.
1e54ecf0681505b1.impact: Nothing changes for residents. This is an internal rulebook about who at city hall can speak or decide for the city, and the debate returns February 6.

1eccd0e76fdd7a74.headline: Water and sewer deal with Meta updated
1eccd0e76fdd7a74.summary: The council approved a third change to the water and sewer agreement with Stadion, LLC — the company known as Meta.
1eccd0e76fdd7a74.impact: This governs the water and sewer service the Meta site gets and on what terms. The motion doesn't say what the change does, so no effect on your household bill is stated.

1edbd9d357577106.headline: Spring Run Plaza approved on 27.35 acres
1edbd9d357577106.summary: The city approved the layout for Spring Run Plaza, a 27.35-acre development at Spring Run Parkway and Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway, starting with six lots.
1edbd9d357577106.impact: If you live or drive near that corner, expect construction on the first 8.15 acres. Two of the lots stay empty until the developer comes back to the city for approval.

1f4a5b99acc0b157.headline: Lot lines redrawn at Saddle Junction
1f4a5b99acc0b157.summary: The council approved an amended plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1, known as the Allgood plat amendment.
1f4a5b99acc0b157.impact: This touches only the property involved. A plat amendment is the paperwork that adjusts how a parcel is drawn on the official map — nothing changes for other residents.

1f8e71c45ed2046f.headline: Taller screening fences where businesses sit above homes
1f8e71c45ed2046f.summary: The council considered measuring fence height from the higher grade of an adjoining commercial or industrial pad, so fences screening homes from businesses can be taller.
1f8e71c45ed2046f.impact: If you live next to a business or industrial site built on higher ground, the fence between you could be built tall enough to actually block the view. Fence rules elsewhere in the city are unchanged.

1ffdeea4575c1804.headline: Gazelle Run application fee cut to $1,350
1ffdeea4575c1804.summary: The council cut the fee for Brett Simpson's Gazelle Run master development plan amendment from $3,350 to $1,350, rather than waiving it entirely as first proposed.
1ffdeea4575c1804.impact: This touches one applicant only. The city collects $2,000 less on this single application, and the fees everyone else pays are unchanged.

2014658e53ffc562.headline: Two items dropped from legislative priorities list
2014658e53ffc562.summary: The council removed two items from its legislative priorities list, one on discontinued zoning and one on transfer of development rights ordinances.
2014658e53ffc562.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this only trims the city's own list of policy priorities.

21312b65de4a2b35.headline: Sign rules now cover city fields and Rodeo Grounds
21312b65de4a2b35.summary: The council rewrote the city's sign rules and defined an "athletic facility" as a high school, middle school, or city-owned regulation field, or the Rodeo Grounds.
21312b65de4a2b35.impact: The sign rules that apply at athletic venues now reach city-owned fields and the Rodeo Grounds, not just school fields. For most residents, day-to-day life is unchanged.

22db0b6251bc32f7.headline: Bid to pause the land sale over water rules fails
22db0b6251bc32f7.summary: The council declined to delay the land-sale resolution while staff refined water requirements and wrote a policy for reviewing future requests to buy city land.
22db0b6251bc32f7.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this was an attempt to hold the sale back for more study, and it did not hold.

239f7e55bff45b15.headline: Consent agenda approved
239f7e55bff45b15.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together without separate discussion; the motion does not list what was included.
239f7e55bff45b15.impact: Nothing here changes for residents on its own — the individual items are listed on the meeting agenda.

24b230adfee0fd6c.headline: Permanent sewer easement released, temporary one kept
24b230adfee0fd6c.summary: The council gave up a permanent sewer easement across a property while holding on to a temporary one.
24b230adfee0fd6c.impact: This is a property-records step between the city and one landowner. The motion doesn't say where the easement is, and nothing changes for residents generally.

25d8c9c542583d2b.headline: Bid to keep 15 acres commercial went nowhere
25d8c9c542583d2b.summary: The council took no action on an alternative version of the land use change that would have preserved roughly 15 acres of commercial land near SR-73 and Airport Road.
25d8c9c542583d2b.impact: Nothing follows from this item on its own — the council adopted the version that converts the full 73 acres, so no commercial land was carved out near the SR-73 and Airport Road intersection.

2775ed0d599459dc.headline: Consent agenda approved
2775ed0d599459dc.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the group of items passed together in a single vote without separate discussion.
2775ed0d599459dc.impact: Nothing changes for residents on its own — this is the routine business the council clears in one vote.

279499360546d485.headline: Consent agenda approved, three items pulled
279499360546d485.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, dropping one item and pulling three others — including the wayfinding signs and the affordable housing plan — out for full discussion.
279499360546d485.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the procedural step that groups routine business into a single vote and sets aside a few items for debate.

2895e8e0ec99fd85.headline: Update the map of land the city could annex
2895e8e0ec99fd85.summary: The council updated its annexation policy plan, extending Area 1 to Utah Lake and requiring the map to mark old boundaries separately from newly expanded ones.
2895e8e0ec99fd85.impact: Nothing changes inside the city today. This matters to owners of unincorporated land on the edges — the council deliberately kept overlaps with neighboring cities so an owner can choose which city to join.

29bbb5872984a679.headline: Parking rules changed for hotels and motels
29bbb5872984a679.summary: The city revised the parking table in its zoning code, changing how many parking spaces hotels, motels, and bed-and-breakfasts must provide.
29bbb5872984a679.impact: Nothing changes day to day for most residents. This affects anyone building or running a hotel, motel, or bed-and-breakfast in Eagle Mountain, who now works from a different parking requirement.

2babc3a20cfdf239.headline: Inland port project area rejected
2babc3a20cfdf239.summary: The council turned down a resolution supporting the creation of a state Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain.
2babc3a20cfdf239.impact: No inland port district moves forward with the city's backing, so the industrial development and tax arrangements that come with one are off the table for now. Day to day, nothing changes.

2bfff6eede2b2165.headline: Jay Johnson joins the Community Services Board
2bfff6eede2b2165.summary: The council appointed Jay Johnson to a one-year term on the Community Services Board, from April 2026 through March 2027.
2bfff6eede2b2165.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer appointment to an advisory board.

2c7564b1969f48a5.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
2c7564b1969f48a5.summary: The council approved its consent agenda — the bundle of uncontested items — after pulling two of the items off it.
2c7564b1969f48a5.impact: Nothing changes for residents on its own. This is the batch vote the council uses to clear routine business in one step.

2e17bbe3fdad07d1.headline: Brandon Park area added to the zoning map
2e17bbe3fdad07d1.summary: The council put the Brandon Park area onto the city's official zoning and future land use maps, recording the zoning designations the area already carries.
2e17bbe3fdad07d1.impact: Nothing changes for Brandon Park property owners — the rules that already applied are now written onto the city's official maps.

2e974bec4ca19318.headline: Wildlife corridor rules put on hold
2e974bec4ca19318.summary: The council delayed a decision on updated wildlife corridor overlay zone rules for Chapter 17.49 of the city code.
2e974bec4ca19318.impact: Nothing changes yet for landowners along the corridor — the existing rules stay in place until the council takes the update back up. Fencing and setback requirements were the sticking point.

2f9f38315e99c875.headline: Meeting end time set at 10:30 PM
2f9f38315e99c875.summary: The council agreed to stop the meeting at 10:30 PM.
2f9f38315e99c875.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is housekeeping about how long the meeting runs.

30068fa852d9b8c2.headline: Meta site road narrowed and redesigned
30068fa852d9b8c2.summary: The city approved a revised street design at the META site, shrinking the sidewalk from 8 feet to 5 and turning the parking lane into a 12-foot drive lane.
30068fa852d9b8c2.impact: If you walk or drive near the META site, the sidewalk will be narrower than originally planned and there will be no on-street parking lane. The 8-foot grass strip becomes a drainage swale instead.

30ffb0a57e413f3c.headline: City manager finalists picked for interviews
30ffb0a57e413f3c.summary: The council settled on its short list of city manager candidates to interview: Rose Beverly, David Fraser, Mike Morris, Steve Mumford, Mark Rooney, and Cliff Strachan.
30ffb0a57e413f3c.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day — this is a step in the hiring process for the city's top administrator, with interviews of these candidates still to come.

3245d5fe1c278c4a.headline: Emily Buss joins the Library Advisory Board
3245d5fe1c278c4a.summary: The council appointed Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board, finishing out a three-year term that runs through December 2027.
3245d5fe1c278c4a.impact: Nothing changes day to day at the library — this fills one seat on the board that advises the city on library matters.

345d6cd48ceee0d2.headline: Lot lines redrawn in Rush Creek industrial area
345d6cd48ceee0d2.summary: The council approved changes to two lots, 102 and 111, in Phase A of the Rush Creek Industrial plat.
345d6cd48ceee0d2.impact: This is a boundary change on paper in an industrial area. It affects the property owner and what can be built on those two lots — not the average resident.

3523e2a88ea7f0a0.headline: Job offer extended for new city manager
3523e2a88ea7f0a0.summary: The council voted to offer someone the city manager job and authorized negotiation of an employment agreement; no name or contract terms were stated in the motion.
3523e2a88ea7f0a0.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day. The city manager is the city's top administrator, so this sets up who will run daily operations once a contract is negotiated and signed.

354136822e2f1afe.headline: Pacific Springs development agreement approved
354136822e2f1afe.summary: The council approved a development agreement for Pacific Springs, the contract setting the terms under which that project can be built.
354136822e2f1afe.impact: The motion itself does not spell out the size, location, or number of homes, so the specifics are in the agreement rather than the vote. It clears the way for the Pacific Springs project to move forward.

3789dc39e9e73310.headline: City land to be sold at $3.44 a square foot
3789dc39e9e73310.summary: The council approved selling a significant piece of city-owned land at $3.44 per square foot, with staff directed to work out the financing terms.
3789dc39e9e73310.impact: The price is set, but the motion does not name the property or the buyer, so what eventually gets built there is still unknown. Staff still has to settle how the buyer pays.

37fb3507f124cf7f.headline: Dani McKean appointed to library board
37fb3507f124cf7f.summary: The council appointed Dani McKean to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board, from January 2026 through December 2028.
37fb3507f124cf7f.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer seat on the board that advises the city on the library.

3804516bb044944b.headline: Rezone a City Center lot to neighborhood commercial
3804516bb044944b.summary: The city rezoned the newly split City Center lot from its 1997 C-1 zoning to Commercial Neighborhood, a more limited commercial zone.
3804516bb044944b.impact: If you live near City Center, this narrows what can open on that lot. The council chose Commercial Neighborhood over the broader zone first proposed because it allows fewer types of business.

38555386e56b9873.headline: Consent agenda approved
38555386e56b9873.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, noting a $47,930 change order on one item and pulling another item for no action.
38555386e56b9873.impact: Nothing changes for residents — the consent agenda is the batch of routine items the council passes together in a single vote.

3906b550937e078f.headline: Mandy Lane appointed to planning commission
3906b550937e078f.summary: The council appointed Mandy Lane to the planning commission for a one-year term through December 2026.
3906b550937e078f.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes day to day. She joins the board that reviews zoning and development proposals before they reach the council.

39890370d9c12d21.headline: Consent agenda approved
39890370d9c12d21.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together in a single vote; the motion does not list what was included.
39890370d9c12d21.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing here changes for residents.

3a02fa5f88f3a3c2.headline: New Alpine School District elementary school approved
3a02fa5f88f3a3c2.summary: The council approved the preliminary plat and site plan for Alpine School District's Elementary 133.
3a02fa5f88f3a3c2.impact: If you live near the site, expect school construction and eventually the traffic a new elementary school brings. This approval clears the way for the district to build.

3bce390e7d1deb27.headline: ShopFest Utah agreement extended to 2035
3bce390e7d1deb27.summary: The council took up an agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce to run the ShopFest Utah event, lengthening the term from five years to ten, through 2035.
3bce390e7d1deb27.impact: Nothing changes day to day. This sets the terms under which the chamber puts on ShopFest, and commits the city to that arrangement through 2035 rather than 2030.

3c545a81a8995e46.headline: Seventh change to last year's budget
3c545a81a8995e46.summary: The council approved the seventh amendment to the 2024-25 budget, adjusting the books before the fiscal year closed.
3c545a81a8995e46.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day — this is the year-end bookkeeping the city does to square its budget with what was actually spent.

3c6cb58d5286dd0d.headline: Rose Ranch agreement without conditions
3c6cb58d5286dd0d.summary: A proposal to approve the Rose Ranch master development agreement without the water conditions was raised but went no further.
3c6cb58d5286dd0d.impact: Nothing changes on its own — this was an alternative to the amended Rose Ranch agreement the council acted on.

3d6b7573482e9255.headline: Cedar Corners land-use map change put off
3d6b7573482e9255.summary: The council delayed a change to the city's future land use map for Cedar Corners Phase 5 and left its public hearing open.
3d6b7573482e9255.impact: Nothing changes yet for the Cedar Corners area — the city's long-range map for the site stays as is, and the hearing remains open for comment.

3f5d7595a2cbb27c.headline: Sweetwater #4 redevelopment plan adopted
3f5d7595a2cbb27c.summary: The council adopted the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area plan as the official plan governing redevelopment in that project area.
3f5d7595a2cbb27c.impact: If you live or own property near Sweetwater #4, this sets the framework for what gets built there and how tax revenue from that growth is reinvested. The motion names no dollar amounts or timeline.

3fb75c7fc7a85b20.headline: Decision on easement rules delayed
3fb75c7fc7a85b20.summary: The council delayed a proposed easement ordinance to November 6, asking the city attorney to define "conservation easement" and set who signs off on easement approvals.
3fb75c7fc7a85b20.impact: Nothing changes for now. The city's existing easement rules stay in place until the council takes the item up again in November.

4015c65a5ef4ad2a.headline: Third change to this year's city budget
4015c65a5ef4ad2a.summary: The council approved a third amendment to the 2025-2026 budget, adjusting the city's spending plan for the fiscal year now ending.
4015c65a5ef4ad2a.impact: The motion doesn't say what was moved or added, so no change to your bills or services is stated — this is the city squaring its books before the year closes.

413db5ca042fc3c5.headline: Ivory Homes agreement approved, water break cut
413db5ca042fc3c5.summary: The city approved an agreement with builder Ivory Homes but removed a proposed break on per-lot water requirements and downgraded promised city benefits to something it "may" consider.
413db5ca042fc3c5.impact: Ivory Homes will have to meet the city's normal water requirement for each lot rather than a reduced one, and any city incentives are now optional rather than guaranteed.

4155fa5e631dc0e5.headline: Jessi Call named Youth Council advisor
4155fa5e631dc0e5.summary: The council appointed Jessi Call as an advisor to the Youth Council Committee, effective immediately and running through June 30, 2026.
4155fa5e631dc0e5.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is an appointment to the committee that guides the city's youth council.

4179c6403f0edf66.headline: Mid-year budget update approved
4179c6403f0edf66.summary: The council approved a second round of amendments to the city's 2025–26 budget; the motion itself names no specific dollar figures.
4179c6403f0edf66.impact: Cities adjust their budgets partway through the year to match actual spending. Nothing in this motion spells out a change residents would notice — the detail sits in the budget document, not the motion.

4233dd274c2fa68c.headline: City manager job offered to a candidate
4233dd274c2fa68c.summary: The council extended a job offer for the city manager position and authorized the mayor to negotiate the employment agreement.
4233dd274c2fa68c.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day, but the city manager is the top staff official who runs city operations, so this sets who will oversee the services you use. The motion does not name the candidate or the pay.

4306735e032f07e3.headline: Porter's Crossing development deal amended
4306735e032f07e3.summary: The council approved a fourth amendment to the master development agreement governing the Porter's Crossing project.
4306735e032f07e3.impact: This changes the terms the city and the developer agreed to for Porter's Crossing. It matters most to people living in or buying near that development; the rest of the city sees no direct change.

43305ee3d9ddd2cb.headline: Pinnacles B-3 site plan put on hold
43305ee3d9ddd2cb.summary: The council set the master site plan for Pinnacles B-3 aside without deciding it.
43305ee3d9ddd2cb.impact: Nothing is settled either way — the plan can come back to the council later. If you live near the Pinnacles area, this only delays the decision.

433adac40200ac3d.headline: Update street cross-section diagrams in city code
433adac40200ac3d.summary: The city updated the right-of-way profile illustrations in its code — the standard diagrams showing how streets are to be laid out.
433adac40200ac3d.impact: Nothing changes day to day. These are the technical drawings engineers and developers follow when designing new streets.

43a6c4ed57a84083.headline: Noise and property nuisance rules rewritten
43a6c4ed57a84083.summary: The council approved changes to the city's nuisance abatement and noise rules, though the motion itself does not spell out what was changed.
43a6c4ed57a84083.impact: These are the rules behind noise complaints and property-upkeep enforcement, so they apply citywide. The motion text doesn't say what changed — read the ordinance before assuming your yard or late-night habits are affected.

43f635c99de0552f.headline: Change the sign-off process for change orders
43f635c99de0552f.summary: The city rewrote its purchasing rules to change how change orders — the cost adjustments made after a contract is already underway — get approved.
43f635c99de0552f.impact: This is internal paperwork and nothing changes for residents. It affects how city staff and the council sign off on added costs for work already under contract.

44fd40041700b17d.headline: Hidden Hollow amenity swap approved
44fd40041700b17d.summary: The city approved a site plan letting the Hidden Hollow development swap amenities for a wellness center, outdoor gathering area, and new fitness equipment.
44fd40041700b17d.impact: If you live in Hidden Hollow, the amenities your neighborhood gets are changing, and the clubhouse must still include at least one amenity. The final terms come back to the council in a written agreement.

4502d3e94a0029a3.headline: Subdivision plat rules amended
4502d3e94a0029a3.summary: The council amended the city's rules for preliminary and final plats — the approval steps land must clear before it can be split into lots.
4502d3e94a0029a3.impact: This changes the process for developers and anyone subdividing land; the motion does not spell out what the new rules require. Existing homeowners see no change.

4718a702504a2186.headline: Study letting people pay the city in bitcoin
4718a702504a2186.summary: The council added a study of whether the city could accept bitcoin as a form of payment to its legislative priorities list.
4718a702504a2186.impact: Nothing changes for you yet — you still cannot pay the city in bitcoin. This only puts the idea on the list of things to look into.

47509f94ec3c8f9b.headline: Political sign rules rewritten
47509f94ec3c8f9b.summary: The council amended the section of the city code that governs political signs; the motion itself does not spell out what the new rules say.
47509f94ec3c8f9b.impact: The rules for putting campaign signs on your own property have changed. If you plan to post signs before an election, check the city's updated sign code rather than assuming the old limits still apply.

48096f2ab8755f8e.headline: Benjamin Perez joins the Library Advisory Board
48096f2ab8755f8e.summary: The council appointed Benjamin Perez to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board, running through 2027.
48096f2ab8755f8e.impact: Nothing changes for library users — this fills one volunteer seat on the board that advises the city on the library.

490e074e93a80f98.headline: Land use map updated for Berry property
490e074e93a80f98.summary: The council took up a matching change to the general plan land use map for the Berry property.
490e074e93a80f98.impact: This is the paperwork that lines the city's long-range map up with the zoning change on the same land. On its own, it changes nothing you would see.

4b5e019b19bb4021.headline: City website contract change order approved
4b5e019b19bb4021.summary: The council approved the first change order on its website contract with WDG, after rewriting a clause about the vendor's budget, timeline, and fees.
4b5e019b19bb4021.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is contract paperwork for the company building the city's website. The reworded clause lets the vendor adjust the final cost or schedule if unknown variables come up.

4b9e8c485db5c455.headline: Emily Hoehne appointed to library board
4b9e8c485db5c455.summary: The council appointed Emily Hoehne to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board, from January 2026 through December 2028.
4b9e8c485db5c455.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer seat on the board that advises the city on the library.

4bb68f5b877246cc.headline: Street width and sidewalk rules put on hold
4bb68f5b877246cc.summary: The council delayed a decision on updated street cross-section rules, asking staff to return with recommendations on curb, gutter and a sidewalk for rural 50-foot streets.
4bb68f5b877246cc.impact: No change yet. Whatever the council settles on would shape how new streets are built — mainly affecting new subdivisions, not existing ones.

4bc107d10a726322.headline: New rules for fences and screening
4bc107d10a726322.summary: The council rewrote the section of city code covering general fencing and screening, changing the rules that apply when property owners put up a fence or wall.
4bc107d10a726322.impact: If you are planning a fence at your home or business, check the updated code before you build — the requirements are not the same as they were.

4be32b7d4441caa0.headline: Sign rule changes put on hold
4be32b7d4441caa0.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's sign rules, which cover what signs are allowed and how sign permits work.
4be32b7d4441caa0.impact: Nothing changes yet — the sign and permit rules on the books today still apply until the council takes the item back up.

4bebdd2be34824da.headline: New school district proposal approved
4bebdd2be34824da.summary: The council approved the proposal to create a new school district and set the date for its final decision on it.
4bebdd2be34824da.impact: This advances the proposal rather than settling it — a final council vote is still to come. If a new district is created, it would change which school district Eagle Mountain belongs to.

4ccee4d22e0cbf66.headline: Adopt a city branding and marketing playbook
4ccee4d22e0cbf66.summary: The council approved the city's brand and marketing playbook and asked for it to come back later with the additions discussed at the meeting.
4ccee4d22e0cbf66.impact: This shapes how the city presents and markets itself. Nothing changes for you day to day.

4cd08b477b5827cf.headline: Consent agenda approved
4cd08b477b5827cf.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, correcting a spelling error in the January 6, 2026 meeting minutes.
4cd08b477b5827cf.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents.

4d14b944f63eedc1.headline: Water and sewer rate changes taken up
4d14b944f63eedc1.summary: The council took up changes to the city's fee schedule for water rates, sewer rates, and utility billing; the record does not show a final outcome.
4d14b944f63eedc1.impact: This is the schedule that sets what you pay on your monthly water and sewer bill. The motion itself does not say how the rates would change, and the record does not show whether it was adopted.

4db177b4f1537563.headline: Rules changed for building into yard setbacks
4db177b4f1537563.summary: The council amended the city code rule governing how far a structure may project into a required yard setback.
4db177b4f1537563.impact: If you are planning to build near your property line, the limits on how far a structure can extend into the setback have changed. The motion itself does not state the new limits — check with the city first.

4f091bf6f56af544.headline: 178 acres proposed for Pole Canyon district
4f091bf6f56af544.summary: The council took up a resolution consenting to the annexation of 178 acres of land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District.
4f091bf6f56af544.impact: This concerns the 178 acres in question and which district serves them, not existing neighborhoods. The meeting record does not show how this one ended.

4f8e82fc4e9e9f1c.headline: Recycling zoning change sent back to staff
4f8e82fc4e9e9f1c.summary: The council pushed back on a set of zoning definition and land-use code changes, directing staff to return with the recycling portion as a 'special use' instead.
4f8e82fc4e9e9f1c.impact: Nothing changes for now. A recycling operation looking to open in Eagle Mountain would have to wait for a revised version of the rules to come back to the council.

5022c0d008fb4a68.headline: Land stays marked commercial on the city map
5022c0d008fb4a68.summary: The council refused to change the general plan for the same two parcels from community commercial and civic/school use to neighborhood housing.
5022c0d008fb4a68.impact: The city's long-range map still shows this land for commercial and civic use, not homes. That is the companion decision to the rezoning denial — together they close the door on this proposal for now.

505321d714b5a33c.headline: Set the rules for hiring a city administrator
505321d714b5a33c.summary: The city adopted the process it will follow to hire its next city administrator, using the standard national guidelines for municipal recruitment.
505321d714b5a33c.impact: This is procedural housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It only settles how the search will be run before anyone is chosen.

510cf9e86add9230.headline: Steve Mumford named interim city administrator
510cf9e86add9230.summary: The council appointed Steve Mumford to run the city's day-to-day operations on an interim basis.
510cf9e86add9230.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day. This temporarily fills the city's top staff job while a permanent hire is worked out.

5152efc76543036a.headline: Long-range land use map updated for Big Eagle 7
5152efc76543036a.summary: The council amended the General Plan's future land use map for the land known as Big Eagle 7.
5152efc76543036a.impact: The General Plan is the city's long-term blueprint for what goes where. This redraws that map for the Big Eagle 7 area; nothing on the ground changes immediately.

5193039e0cf72edb.headline: Council members assigned to city boards for 2024
5193039e0cf72edb.summary: The council set its 2024 board assignments: Burnham to cemetery and arts, Clark to seniors and library, Gray to veterans, parks and youth, Wood to economic development, Wright to planning.
5193039e0cf72edb.impact: This tells you which council member to contact about a given topic — Wright for planning issues, Clark for the library or senior center, Gray for parks. Nothing else changes.

51d7e3eb20aea2aa.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 development deal approved
51d7e3eb20aea2aa.summary: The city approved a development agreement for Cedar Corners Phase 5, with conditions on when construction may start and on connecting the roads and sidewalks.
51d7e3eb20aea2aa.impact: If you live near Poplar Drive or Maple Street, the developer must connect the roads on both sides and keep the walkways continuous rather than leaving them to dead-end.

51ea4965b8e28a32.headline: Property tax increase heads to a hearing
51ea4965b8e28a32.summary: The council took up a resolution declaring the city's intent to raise property tax revenue, give public notice, and set the required Truth-in-Taxation hearing date.
51ea4965b8e28a32.impact: If the increase goes ahead, homeowners would pay more. The Truth-in-Taxation hearing is the point where you can speak before the council settles on a final rate.

524eaaf50b91ac01.headline: Three items pulled for fuller discussion
524eaaf50b91ac01.summary: The council pulled the Eagle Square plat, the wayfinding sign contract, and the marketing contract out of the consent agenda for separate discussion.
524eaaf50b91ac01.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the procedural step that moved three items out of the quick-approval batch so they could be debated individually.

532ed6460234c068.headline: Fence rule changes put on hold
532ed6460234c068.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's fencing rules and sent them back for discussion at a future work session.
532ed6460234c068.impact: The current fence rules still apply — nothing changes for your yard yet. The proposal is expected to come back at a later meeting.

538d097678f79cb6.headline: Porter's Crossing lot rezoned from open space to housing
538d097678f79cb6.summary: The council rezoned one lot in Porter's Crossing from open space to R1, the city's single-family housing zone.
538d097678f79cb6.impact: A parcel that was set aside as open space can now hold a house. If you live next to that lot in Porter's Crossing, expect a home there instead of undeveloped ground.

53ad04727b025886.headline: Routine items passed in one vote
53ad04727b025886.summary: The council approved its consent agenda — land and equipment purchases, two bond releases, meeting minutes, and two treasurer appointments — pulling two items out for separate discussion.
53ad04727b025886.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. The recruiting-consultant contract was one of the items pulled out.

54e5838afc15ab7b.headline: Water conservation plan added to the General Plan
54e5838afc15ab7b.summary: The city adopted a Water Use and Preservation Plan as an appendix to its 2018 General Plan, setting out how Eagle Mountain will manage water.
54e5838afc15ab7b.impact: Nothing changes on your water bill or in your yard today. The plan is the policy the city will point to in future decisions about water and growth.

54f80eaa76e263d7.headline: City land sold at $2.07 a square foot
54f80eaa76e263d7.summary: The city approved selling part of a city-owned parcel in Utah County at $2.07 per square foot, with the buyer paying all related costs.
54f80eaa76e263d7.impact: Most residents will notice nothing. The buyer covers the survey and other fees, so the sale costs the city nothing and moves a piece of public land into private hands.

5540a62cc4c397eb.headline: Consent agenda approved, four items pulled
5540a62cc4c397eb.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling items 12.A, 12.B, 12.C and 13.C out for separate discussion.
5540a62cc4c397eb.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. The four pulled items were debated one at a time instead of being passed in a batch.

556b6e9e5b47cb85.headline: Mayor's powers ordinance held over
556b6e9e5b47cb85.summary: The council delayed a decision on rewriting the section of city code that spells out the mayor's powers and duties.
556b6e9e5b47cb85.impact: Nothing changes day to day — the mayor's current authority stays in place until the council returns to this item.

55974898ac3a2e40.headline: Elizabeth Evans joins Community Services Board
55974898ac3a2e40.summary: The council appointed Elizabeth Evans to the Community Services Board for a term running April 2026 through March 2027.
55974898ac3a2e40.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. This fills another seat on the advisory board, this one for a single year.

560b169a35ad1ebf.headline: Consent agenda approved, December minutes fixed
560b169a35ad1ebf.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulled one item to be taken up later, and corrected the vote recorded in the December 16 minutes.
560b169a35ad1ebf.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. The item that was pulled will come back on a future agenda.

5695a6d9110c0094.headline: City drops ADU impact-fee item from lobbying list
5695a6d9110c0094.summary: The city removed the item on impact fees for accessory dwelling units from the list of priorities it asks the state legislature to act on.
5695a6d9110c0094.impact: Nothing changes for residents or for what you pay to build an ADU — the city simply stopped asking the legislature to take up the issue this session.

57c05393cf0231a9.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled out
57c05393cf0231a9.summary: The council approved its bundle of routine consent items but pulled the Mountainland Supply development agreement out for separate discussion.
57c05393cf0231a9.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the batch of routine business the council passes in a single vote, minus the one item it wanted to debate on its own.

57f21752fea7182a.headline: Mid-year budget adjustment
57f21752fea7182a.summary: The city made its fourth round of adjustments to the 2024-2025 budget.
57f21752fea7182a.impact: This is the mid-year bookkeeping the city does to true up its budget. The motion doesn't say which line items moved or by how much, so nothing here points to a change you would notice.

5936c4caca332e82.headline: Land rezoned for the new elementary school
5936c4caca332e82.summary: The council rezoned the land for Alpine School District's Elementary 133 so the school can be built there.
5936c4caca332e82.impact: Paired with the site plan approval, this lets the school district move ahead. Neighbors will get a school on that land instead of whatever the previous zoning allowed.

59b6a42a3fe950c7.headline: Less water required from builders for new homes
59b6a42a3fe950c7.summary: The city cut the water rights developers must turn over per new home, dropping the indoor requirement from 0.53 to 0.34 acre-feet, and ordering a study of apartment water use.
59b6a42a3fe950c7.impact: This lands on developers, not on your water bill. It follows the city's smaller lawn requirements, so new yards will have less sod. The council also wants a closer look at how much water apartments actually use.

5a3d6e06075bce86.headline: Building standards for homes updated
5a3d6e06075bce86.summary: The council changed the city code's definition of a "structure" and its residential development standards table.
5a3d6e06075bce86.impact: If you are planning to build on your lot, the rules for what counts as a structure and the standards your project must meet have shifted. The motion itself doesn't spell out the specifics.

5a71a5e9f46f3f42.headline: April named Financial Literacy Month
5a71a5e9f46f3f42.summary: The council proclaimed April as Financial Literacy Month in Eagle Mountain.
5a71a5e9f46f3f42.impact: Ceremonial only — nothing changes for residents, and no city money or program is committed.

5a862c799932541e.headline: Wildfire-risk map adopted for the city
5a862c799932541e.summary: The city adopted an official map of the areas where homes sit against wildland fire risk, and updated the related code chapter that governs them.
5a862c799932541e.impact: If your property falls inside the mapped wildland interface area, the city's Chapter 15.95 rules apply to it. The map is what decides whether you are in or out of that zone.

5af4b66ae66d70d0.headline: Animal rules sent back for more work
5af4b66ae66d70d0.summary: The council sent proposed rules on alternative animal management plans, and the zoning that goes with them, back to the Planning Commission for further review.
5af4b66ae66d70d0.impact: If you keep animals on your property, nothing changes yet. The rules are still being rewritten and will have to come back to the council before anything takes effect.

5bd1eae88ffc55e4.headline: Fence rules rewritten, including chain link
5bd1eae88ffc55e4.summary: The council took up changes to the city's fence rules, covering definitions, privacy fencing, general fencing standards, and chain link fencing.
5bd1eae88ffc55e4.impact: Fence rules govern what you can put up around your own yard. The motion does not spell out what changed, so check the current code with the city before building a fence.

5c36ec68d1455668.headline: Consent agenda approved
5c36ec68d1455668.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items voted through together without separate discussion.
5c36ec68d1455668.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents.

5c7179c232e1bd11.headline: Overland development changes put on hold
5c7179c232e1bd11.summary: The council delayed a decision on the fifth amendment to the Overland master development agreement and will take it up at a future meeting.
5c7179c232e1bd11.impact: Nothing changes for now — the existing Overland agreement stays as written until the council revisits the amendment.

5d416daeb9ba7649.headline: MHTN Architects hired to plan a downtown
5d416daeb9ba7649.summary: The city hired MHTN Architects to create the Downtown Master Plan, choosing the firm after hearing pitches from three competing firms.
5d416daeb9ba7649.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. This hires the firm that will draft the city's vision for a downtown, work that would shape what eventually gets built there.

5d49dfe012c02128.headline: Tax increase figures formally acknowledged
5d49dfe012c02128.summary: The council acknowledged the budget officer's statement of the proposed property tax increase and the schedule showing what that increase would cost taxpayers.
5d49dfe012c02128.impact: Nothing changes yet. This is a step state law requires before a city can raise property taxes; the real decision comes later at the public hearing.

5d510b7d1c66c4b0.headline: Setback measuring change delayed
5d510b7d1c66c4b0.summary: The council put off a change to how the city measures setbacks on site plans, measuring from the existing right-of-way instead of the curb.
5d510b7d1c66c4b0.impact: Nothing changes for now. The current measuring rules stay in place for anyone submitting a site plan until the council takes the item up again.

5e74fce9df30e88f.headline: Franchise deal approved with Zayo Group
5e74fce9df30e88f.summary: The city approved a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, LLC, the standard permission a telecom company needs to do business in Eagle Mountain.
5e74fce9df30e88f.impact: Nothing changes for you today. The motion does not say what Zayo will build or when — this is the paperwork step that lets the company operate in the city.

5fb5011ae1896332.headline: Mid-year budget update approved
5fb5011ae1896332.summary: The council approved the fifth amendment to the city's 2024-2025 budget, adjusting the spending plan partway through the fiscal year.
5fb5011ae1896332.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the bookkeeping the city does to keep its budget lined up with actual spending. No dollar figures were stated in the motion.

5fc15cb5f1f35b35.headline: Hidden Hollow amenity swap put on hold
5fc15cb5f1f35b35.summary: The council delayed a decision on a minor change to the amenities planned for the Hidden Hollow development.
5fc15cb5f1f35b35.impact: If you live in or are buying into Hidden Hollow, the proposed change to the development's amenities is still unsettled and will come back to the council later.

6015205d292e2355.headline: Youth court and justice court added to priority list
6015205d292e2355.summary: The council added a youth court, a justice court, and other public safety measures to the city's list of legislative priorities.
6015205d292e2355.impact: Nothing changes yet. This only puts these ideas on the city's priority list — an actual youth or justice court would take separate decisions later.

602453a88b2b3bf1.headline: RAP tax question goes to voters in November
602453a88b2b3bf1.summary: The council put a 0.1% sales tax for recreation, arts, and cultural facilities on the November 4, 2025 ballot.
602453a88b2b3bf1.impact: You decide this one at the polls. If it passes, you would pay an extra 10 cents on every $100 spent in the city, with the money going to recreation and cultural facilities.

607b97fa29efc741.headline: Decision on lot-size rules pushed to March
607b97fa29efc741.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to lot size mixture and residential development standards, sending staff back to collect council feedback before the March 6, 2024 meeting.
607b97fa29efc741.impact: Nothing changes yet. If you follow how large lots in new subdivisions have to be, the rules come back to the council on March 6 — that's the next chance to weigh in.

607b9c8ee0b238e7.headline: Lone Tree road funding added to priorities list
607b9c8ee0b238e7.summary: The council added a funding plan for roads serving the Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to its legislative priorities list.
607b9c8ee0b238e7.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. This puts the road funding on the city's official ask list; any actual money and construction would still have to be approved later.

60f7e94413bd6b60.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled out
60f7e94413bd6b60.summary: The council approved its consent agenda and pulled the downtown plan and inland port resolutions out for separate discussion later in the meeting.
60f7e94413bd6b60.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. Its only effect was that two bigger items got debated on their own instead of being passed in a batch.

610608cbb6ff22dc.headline: Parking rule changes rejected
610608cbb6ff22dc.summary: The council moved to reject proposed changes to the city's parking rules.
610608cbb6ff22dc.impact: The parking rules stay exactly as they are today. There is nothing new you need to do, and no new restrictions on where you park.

6122b537a87857d2.headline: Jason Allen joins the planning commission
6122b537a87857d2.summary: The council signed off on appointing Jason Allen to the planning commission for a three-year term running January 2026 through December 2028.
6122b537a87857d2.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day. The planning commission reviews building and zoning proposals before they reach the council, so who sits on it shapes what gets built.

618b542767654bae.headline: Site plan approved for LKL Associates
618b542767654bae.summary: The council approved a site plan for LKL Associates; the record does not say what the project is or where it would go.
618b542767654bae.impact: The record is too thin to say who this touches. A site plan approval is the step that lets a developer move ahead with building on a lot.

62e0b763f54dc1c3.headline: Affordable housing fund set up
62e0b763f54dc1c3.summary: The city created a separate Affordable Housing Fund to hold money earmarked for affordable housing, with a small wording fix changing "adopted" to "received."
62e0b763f54dc1c3.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this creates the account, not the spending. How much goes in and what it pays for would be decided later.

639bc4a985b55efa.headline: Developer trees, $40K for parks, calendar tweaks
639bc4a985b55efa.summary: The council approved its consent items but required Stadion LLC to donate trees or cash, added a $40,000 Comcast payment for parks, and revised the 2024 meeting calendar.
639bc4a985b55efa.impact: The $40,000 from Comcast is set aside for park improvements, and the developer's trees will be planted elsewhere in the city. If you follow council meetings, the March 5 meeting is gone and March 6 and November 6 were added.

64d01d1c7d363b27.headline: Rose Ranch farmland-to-housing rezone
64d01d1c7d363b27.summary: The council weighed rezoning Rose Ranch from agriculture to the R2 and R3 housing zones, conditioned on crosswalks, a historical marker and finishing the Pony Express Trail.
64d01d1c7d363b27.impact: If it goes ahead, farmland at Rose Ranch becomes housing. Neighbors would get raised tabletop crosswalks and a historical marker on the Pony Express Trail, and the trail finished as usable space.

652689e1ffe0a542.headline: Easier lot line changes between neighbors
652689e1ffe0a542.summary: The city allowed a property line between a subdivision and a neighboring parcel to be moved by survey instead of a full plat amendment.
652689e1ffe0a542.impact: If you own property and want to shift a boundary with a neighbor, the process is now shorter. The city will also record a notice on the property so owners can tell when a parcel sits in more than one zone.

65282e306887a4aa.headline: Site plan rules updated for new development
65282e306887a4aa.summary: The council updated the city's site plan rules but left out a proposed change covering the swap of one approved exterior building material for another.
65282e306887a4aa.impact: This touches builders and businesses going through site plan review, who must still get sign-off to change approved exterior materials. If you are not developing property, nothing changes for you.

662b66a778b2744e.headline: City budget amended to $156 million
662b66a778b2744e.summary: The council amended this year's city budget for the third time, setting the total at $155,990,118.
662b66a778b2744e.impact: This sets the ceiling on what the city can spend this budget year. The motion doesn't say what the money is for, so you won't see a specific change from this vote alone.

66f968a18f760bd1.headline: City buys 21 acres for a future civic campus
66f968a18f760bd1.summary: The city agreed to buy 20.99 acres of land from Ivory Homes and SITLA for a future civic campus.
66f968a18f760bd1.impact: The city now has land set aside for future civic buildings. Nothing is built yet — the motion doesn't say what will go there, what it cost, or when.

6777498a8c4a84b0.headline: Move to reject fence rules found no support
6777498a8c4a84b0.summary: A proposal to reject the fencing code changes outright drew no support and died without coming to a vote.
6777498a8c4a84b0.impact: Nothing changes for residents. The fencing rules were neither rejected nor adopted here, and this proposal never reached a vote.

6820f051bcd1f4fd.headline: Brett Wright named mayor pro tempore for 2025
6820f051bcd1f4fd.summary: The council named Councilmember Brett Wright as mayor pro tempore for 2025.
6820f051bcd1f4fd.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this simply decides who leads a council meeting when the mayor cannot be there.

69540fc766428341.headline: New city website, built for $135,000
69540fc766428341.summary: The city hired Web Development Group (WDG) Platforms to build a new city website for $135,000, with staff left to settle the payment schedule.
69540fc766428341.impact: Expect a redesigned city website at some point — the motion does not say when. Nothing else changes for you, and the $135,000 is city money, not a new charge to residents.

698027249424544a.headline: Subdivision review deadlines tied to state law
698027249424544a.summary: The city rewrote its code so deadlines for reviewing subdivision plans point to state law instead of a fixed number of days.
698027249424544a.impact: Routine housekeeping for builders and planning staff. Nothing changes for residents.

6a82f26c55489d7a.headline: Change to home-building rules rejected
6a82f26c55489d7a.summary: The council turned down a proposed change to the city's definitions and residential development standards, leaving the current rules for building homes in place.
6a82f26c55489d7a.impact: Nothing changes — the rules governing what can be built on residential lots stay as they are, and builders and homeowners keep working under the existing standards.

6acdb3566ea57bbe.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook land use change delayed
6acdb3566ea57bbe.summary: The council delayed a decision on changing the long-range land use map for the land known as Cedar Valley Holbrook.
6acdb3566ea57bbe.impact: Nothing changes — this map change was set aside along with the related rezoning and will return to the council later.

6b2b79b9c30c7af2.headline: Consent agenda approved
6b2b79b9c30c7af2.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote, with a change to one item that had been discussed earlier in the work session.
6b2b79b9c30c7af2.impact: This is routine housekeeping — the consent agenda is where the council batches items it does not need to debate one by one.

6bf94fddada9f71d.headline: One lot rezoned in Meadow Ranch
6bf94fddada9f71d.summary: The council approved a zoning change for a single property, Lot 433 in Meadow Ranch Plat 4.
6bf94fddada9f71d.impact: This affects one lot and its immediate neighbors, not the wider city. The motion does not say what the new zoning allows, so check with the city if you live nearby.

6c01b4fe054e32f4.headline: McDonald's plan paused for a traffic study
6c01b4fe054e32f4.summary: The council put the McDonald's site plan at City Center on hold until a traffic study is completed.
6c01b4fe054e32f4.impact: The City Center McDonald's cannot be approved until traffic near the site is studied, so the project is pushed back. Nothing changes on the ground in the meantime.

6c26283e0e57f64f.headline: Consent items approved; school site plan sent back
6c26283e0e57f64f.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items — bond releases, minutes, the 2023 audit and site plans — but sent the middle school site plan back over an easement.
6c26283e0e57f64f.impact: Mostly housekeeping. The one item to watch: the Alpine School District middle school on Belle Street did not get its final sign-off, because the council wants an easement question settled first.

6cb716530b38110c.headline: Lennar put on notice over Ault Farms agreement
6cb716530b38110c.summary: The city formally notified Lennar Homes that it is in default on specific terms of the Ault Farms master development agreement.
6cb716530b38110c.impact: If you live in or near Ault Farms, this is the city pressing the builder to meet commitments it agreed to. The motion doesn't say which terms were missed or what happens next.

6d42d7a9159be015.headline: New rules to shift development rights between sites
6d42d7a9159be015.summary: The city created a transfer of development rights overlay zone, a tool that lets building density be moved from one property to another.
6d42d7a9159be015.impact: This mostly matters to landowners and developers: it opens a path to shift allowed homes off one parcel and onto another, which means density can land in different places than the base zoning suggests.

6e456e4d7c5e00b5.headline: Consent agenda approved, with trails added
6e456e4d7c5e00b5.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, adding "trails" to the scope of review in one of the items it covered.
6e456e4d7c5e00b5.impact: This is routine housekeeping — the consent agenda bundles uncontested items into one vote, and nothing here changes for residents.

6eb156bed489b878.headline: Transportation Master Plan adopted
6eb156bed489b878.summary: The council adopted the Transportation Master Plan, the city's long-range blueprint for which roads Eagle Mountain builds and widens as it grows.
6eb156bed489b878.impact: Nothing changes on your street tomorrow, but this plan is what the city points to when deciding which roads get built or widened and what developers must put in.
