6f0bff804a840759.headline: Harmony 13 subdivision plan denied
6f0bff804a840759.summary: The council rejected the preliminary plat — the proposed lot layout — for the Harmony 13 subdivision.
6f0bff804a840759.impact: As drawn, Harmony 13 does not move forward. That touches the developer and neighbors near the site; the motion itself gives no reasons for the denial.

6f2ce38fdefe909d.headline: City fee schedule updated
6f2ce38fdefe909d.summary: The council approved changes to Appendix A of the city's consolidated fee schedule, the price list for city services and permits.
6f2ce38fdefe909d.impact: Some of what you pay the city changes. The motion does not say which fees or by how much, so check the current schedule before pulling a permit or paying for a city service.

6f8197042b5d4524.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
6f8197042b5d4524.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled the Transportation Master Plan and a fee reduction request out for separate discussion.
6f8197042b5d4524.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the housekeeping step that clears routine items in one vote and sets two aside for fuller debate.

7057ff3826d426d1.headline: Hidden Hollow keeps its pool
7057ff3826d426d1.summary: The council rejected Cadence Homes' request to swap the planned swimming pool at the Hidden Hollow clubhouse for a gym and lawn games.
7057ff3826d426d1.impact: If you live in or are buying into Hidden Hollow, the clubhouse amenity stays as it was originally approved — a swimming pool, not a gym.

705a43342717c003.headline: December named Utah PTA Centennial month
705a43342717c003.summary: The council proclaimed December 2025 as Utah PTA Centennial Celebration Month.
705a43342717c003.impact: This is ceremonial — nothing changes for residents. It's a public nod to the PTA's 100th anniversary.

724181ab2d215bdd.headline: Youth Council vote redone to include the mayor
724181ab2d215bdd.summary: The council reopened its vote on the Youth Council rules after the city attorney said city code requires the mayor to be included in it.
724181ab2d215bdd.impact: This is a procedural do-over to make the vote valid. The ordinance itself did not change, and nothing changes for residents.

72c2bf4a2d8fdc5c.headline: Rezone of Village Core land rejected
72c2bf4a2d8fdc5c.summary: The council turned down a request to rezone two parcels from village core commercial and community open space to a residential zone.
72c2bf4a2d8fdc5c.impact: The land keeps its current commercial and open-space zoning, so the housing proposed there cannot move forward as filed. Nothing changes for neighbors nearby.

72c99c3d5fc55f98.headline: Telecom rules added to council's priority list
72c99c3d5fc55f98.summary: The council added drafting a telecommunications ordinance and/or franchise agreement to its list of legislative priorities.
72c99c3d5fc55f98.impact: Nothing changes for you yet — this puts the item on the city's to-do list, and any actual rules would have to come back to the council later.

734dfd285cc9605e.headline: New recreation, arts, and parks tax created
734dfd285cc9605e.summary: The city wrote a new Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax into its municipal code, adding a chapter that establishes the tax.
734dfd285cc9605e.impact: This puts the tax on the books. The motion itself doesn't state a rate or a start date, so check the ordinance for what you would actually pay and when.

742f29587bd6c256.headline: Angeline Washburn appointed to Youth Council
742f29587bd6c256.summary: The council appointed Angeline Washburn as a Youth Council Advisory for a one-year term through June 2025.
742f29587bd6c256.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills another volunteer advisory seat on the city's youth council.

747ebedc1ff0caed.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled for debate
747ebedc1ff0caed.summary: The council approved its batch of routine consent items, pulling two of them out to be taken up separately.
747ebedc1ff0caed.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents.

77b630b74967d885.headline: Emily Hoehne joins the Library Advisory Board
77b630b74967d885.summary: The council appointed Emily Hoehne to the Library Advisory Board for a term running through December 31, 2025.
77b630b74967d885.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a seat on the volunteer board that advises on the library, through the end of the year.

79609f4529811ca5.headline: New standards for RV and trailer storage
79609f4529811ca5.summary: The council rewrote the city's rules for outdoor storage of recreational vehicles and trailers, changing the standards that apply to that use.
79609f4529811ca5.impact: This touches properties used to store RVs and trailers outdoors — storage yard owners and operators more than ordinary homeowners. The record doesn't spell out the new requirements, so check the updated chapter before relying on the old rules.

7a165bf8fcb02408.headline: Overland development deal amended, lights capped at 25 feet
7a165bf8fcb02408.summary: The city approved a change to the Overland development agreement, requiring 25-foot light poles instead of 30-foot and a finished 35-acre land swap with the state.
7a165bf8fcb02408.impact: If you live near the Overland project, outdoor lighting will sit five feet lower than planned, which means less glare. The deal also depends on a state land exchange tied to the planned bypass road.

7bba93771e07f46e.headline: Energy code changes put on hold
7bba93771e07f46e.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's energy-related building and land use rules in Title 17.
7bba93771e07f46e.impact: Nothing changes for now — the existing rules stay in place until the council brings the item back.

7bbbf065a021484c.headline: Site plan approved for Firefly plats 4 and 5
7bbbf065a021484c.summary: The city approved the site plan for Firefly NPA 1A, plats 4 and 5, in the southwest part of the city near Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway and Pole Canyon Boulevard.
7bbbf065a021484c.impact: If you live in the southwest end of the city, expect building on this parcel to move ahead. The motion does not say how many homes or lots are involved.

7bf90f6f13018de0.headline: Marian Burningham appointed to Cemetery Advisory Board
7bf90f6f13018de0.summary: The council appointed Marian Burningham to a three-year term on the Cemetery Advisory Board, running through December 31, 2027.
7bf90f6f13018de0.impact: Nothing changes for residents — the board advises the city on the cemetery, and this simply fills a seat on it.

7c86c8b984ecdcee.headline: Change order on the sewer plant upgrade
7c86c8b984ecdcee.summary: The council approved a change order with engineering firm Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services for the wastewater treatment plant upgrade.
7c86c8b984ecdcee.impact: This adjusts the engineering contract on the city's sewer plant upgrade. You will not see anything different at home; the plant work continues under revised terms.

7ca89e1d86abe0a3.headline: Changes to the Ault Farms (Parkway Fields) development deal
7ca89e1d86abe0a3.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the Ault Farms (Parkway Fields) master development agreement, adding a nine-month sunset clause to the amendment.
7ca89e1d86abe0a3.impact: This touches the Parkway Fields area rather than the city at large, and the amended terms expire after nine months. The motion itself does not say what else in the agreement changed.

7d6eda8f4284ed04.headline: Revised plan for Town Center marketplace
7d6eda8f4284ed04.summary: The council approved an amended preliminary plat for the Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center.
7d6eda8f4284ed04.impact: This is an early planning step for the Town Center marketplace, laying out how the land is divided. Nothing gets built on this approval alone.

7e051171013c9991.headline: Consent agenda approved
7e051171013c9991.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together without separate discussion.
7e051171013c9991.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the routine bundle of items the council clears in one vote.

7ebb1a9627558b14.headline: City backs an inland port project area
7ebb1a9627558b14.summary: The council formally supported creating a Utah Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain, a development designation created under state law.
7ebb1a9627558b14.impact: This is the city's show of support, not the final word — the state port authority decides whether the project area happens. Nothing changes on the ground yet.

7f0c6df5efdcea0a.headline: ShaRee Curtis joins Community Services Board
7f0c6df5efdcea0a.summary: The council appointed ShaRee Curtis to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, from April 2026 through March 2028.
7f0c6df5efdcea0a.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer appointment to an advisory board.

7fa70e7d9e820261.headline: Nathan Washburn appointed to Youth Council
7fa70e7d9e820261.summary: The council appointed Nathan Washburn as a Youth Council Advisory for a one-year term through June 2025.
7fa70e7d9e820261.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a volunteer advisory seat on the city's youth council.

8023ac051bf7cc07.headline: Fence and retaining wall rules put on hold
8023ac051bf7cc07.summary: The council delayed a decision on new rules for privacy fences, landscaping buffers, and retaining walls.
8023ac051bf7cc07.impact: Nothing changes for now — the current fence and wall rules still apply. If you were waiting on the new standards before building, you will have to wait longer.

806ae8c9a1412570.headline: Block grant money set: $150K for small businesses
806ae8c9a1412570.summary: The city set its 2026 federal block grant spending: $150,000 in small business grants, $36,163 for yard cleanup, $20,000 for an ADA crosswalk, and $35,292 in aid programs.
806ae8c9a1412570.impact: Small businesses can apply for grant money, and lower-income households get help with utility bills, cemetery costs, school supplies, food and yard cleanup. A new ADA ramp and crosswalk is funded at Fiona Street and Airport Road.

806e6799f0ba53b4.headline: Jacob Adams appointed to Youth Council
806e6799f0ba53b4.summary: The council appointed Jacob Adams to the Youth Council for a term running through June 30, 2025.
806e6799f0ba53b4.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a seat on the city's youth advisory body.

807b264076c36dee.headline: Marian Burningham joins Community Services Board
807b264076c36dee.summary: The council appointed Marian Burningham to the Community Services Board for a term running April 2026 through March 2029.
807b264076c36dee.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. This fills one seat on an advisory board.

80cc314a6931926d.headline: Berry property rezoned for foothill homes
80cc314a6931926d.summary: The city rezoned the land known as the Berry property from agriculture to foothill residential, opening it to housing.
80cc314a6931926d.impact: The land can now be developed as foothill housing instead of staying farmland. Neighbors should expect a housing project to move forward there, though the motion sets no timeline or number of homes.

80e8c83b7c065688.headline: City hall design made a top city priority
80e8c83b7c065688.summary: The council moved the city hall land purchase and a mortgage assistance program to its completed list and made designing a city hall a high priority downtown.
80e8c83b7c065688.impact: Nothing changes for you yet. This is the city's internal to-do list, and it now flags designing a city hall within the first phase of the downtown plan as a top item.

81ba05b85bb5aab4.headline: Split a City Center commercial lot in two
81ba05b85bb5aab4.summary: The city approved dividing Lot 1 of the City Center Commercial property, creating one more lot for commercial use.
81ba05b85bb5aab4.impact: Nothing opens yet. This is the paperwork that lets the owner divide the property, and anything built there still needs its own approval.

82662ff9bde0930c.headline: Open space plan adopted, backyard trail dropped
82662ff9bde0930c.summary: The council adopted the city's natural open space and wildlife habitat plan, but cut a walking path planned behind homes between Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane.
82662ff9bde0930c.impact: Homeowners along Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane will not get a path behind their backyards, though the land stays classified as open space. The plan also drops its semi-truck parking language and lets goat grazing run as needed rather than on a fixed schedule.

8296592ec7cf7407.headline: Up to 20.35 acres near Bypass Road to be traded
8296592ec7cf7407.summary: The council approved disposing of up to 20.35 acres of city-owned land known as the Bypass Road Property, to be exchanged for land chosen later.
8296592ec7cf7407.impact: The city is clearing the way to swap this land, but has not yet said what it will get in return. Staff must come back to the council before any trade is final.

832f461559fb6318.headline: 10% of new homes in some zones must be affordable
832f461559fb6318.summary: The city now requires at least 10% of new homes in certain residential zones to be priced for households earning 80% or less of Utah County's median income.
832f461559fb6318.impact: If you build or buy in these zones, a share of the homes carry a recorded deed restriction: the owner must live there and the price is capped. Applies to new development, not existing homes.

843d1280437f391d.headline: Parks plan adopted, Sweetwater Park added
843d1280437f391d.summary: The city adopted its parks, trails and open space master plan along with the impact fee plan that pays for it, adding Sweetwater Park's cost to the list.
843d1280437f391d.impact: This is the city's list of parks and trails it intends to build, and the fees charged on new construction that fund them. Sweetwater Park is now part of that funded list.

84ddbf698a381613.headline: Public art rules changed
84ddbf698a381613.summary: The council approved changes to the city's public art rules in Chapter 12.35 of the municipal code.
84ddbf698a381613.impact: The record doesn't say what changed. The chapter governs how the city handles public art, so there's no stated change to what you pay or do.

857d6838d22c07be.headline: Housing data and new road corridors added to priorities
857d6838d22c07be.summary: The council added two items to its legislative priorities list: gathering citywide housing data, and planning new road corridors on the city's south and west sides.
857d6838d22c07be.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet — this only tells city staff and state lawmakers what to work on. Any actual road or housing decision would come back to the council later.

86c9c93aa846efb7.headline: Push to allow archery at the Rodeo Grounds
86c9c93aa846efb7.summary: The council added allowing archery shooting at the city's Rodeo Grounds to its legislative priorities list.
86c9c93aa846efb7.impact: Nothing changes at the Rodeo Grounds for now. This puts archery on the city's list of things to pursue; it does not by itself open a place to shoot.

86d5a3525b0cf554.headline: Rec center funding pulled, $1M pooled for parks
86d5a3525b0cf554.summary: The council reworked how proceeds from the utility sale are spent, moving $2.6 million earmarked for a recreation center into unallocated funds and pooling $1 million for parks.
86d5a3525b0cf554.impact: A recreation center is off the funding list for now — council members said it could be revisited later, possibly starting with buying land. The $1 million park fund still covers Silver Lake amphitheater, bike park, and Nolan Park improvements.

884b312d354f5469.headline: Hillside building rules put on hold
884b312d354f5469.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's rules for building on slopes and hillsides.
884b312d354f5469.impact: If you own or plan to build on a hillside lot, the current slope rules still apply. Nothing changes until the council revisits this.

8911703b3b2ae71b.headline: Development deal set for Spring Run Plaza
8911703b3b2ae71b.summary: The council approved the master development agreement for Spring Run Plaza, capping the required landscaping width at 10 feet and allowing engineered retaining walls taller than 6 feet without tiering.
8911703b3b2ae71b.impact: This sets the rules the developer must build to at that corner. You may see tall, untiered retaining walls there, though stacked boulder and rock walls are not allowed.

89860402b8caa537.headline: New rules for building on steep slopes
89860402b8caa537.summary: The city rewrote four sections of its code governing development on steep slopes, changing how hillside land may be built on.
89860402b8caa537.impact: If you own hillside land or plan to build on a slope, the rules for what you can put there have changed. Residents on flatter ground are unaffected.

8a6b740387bed2d3.headline: Hire a consultant to study Eagle's Landing
8a6b740387bed2d3.summary: The city hired Economic & Planning Systems to run a market study for Eagle's Landing, a large commercial project planned on Pony Express Parkway north of downtown.
8a6b740387bed2d3.impact: Nothing changes for you now. The study, expected to take one to three months, will help the city decide whether to use a TIF bond to pay for roads and utilities at the site.

8aaadeedeeeb1a16.headline: Remaining consent items approved
8aaadeedeeeb1a16.summary: The council approved the three consent items it had set aside for a separate vote — items 10.A, 10.B and 12.A.
8aaadeedeeeb1a16.impact: Nothing changes for residents from this step itself — it is the follow-up vote on items pulled out of the batch. The motion does not say what those items contain.

8aea3cf68abd26db.headline: Zayo fiber franchise agreement put on hold
8aea3cf68abd26db.summary: The council delayed a decision on a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, LLC, a fiber network company.
8aea3cf68abd26db.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now — the agreement was set aside and will come back to the council another night.

8ca676754311bed6.headline: Residential zoning rules queued for review
8ca676754311bed6.summary: The council added a review of the city's residential zoning rules, Municipal Code Chapter 17.25, to its list of legislative priorities.
8ca676754311bed6.impact: Nothing changes yet — this only puts residential zoning on the council's to-do list. Any actual change to what can be built in a residential zone would be a separate decision later.

8d133968ed8a08d2.headline: Public comment moved later in the meeting
8d133968ed8a08d2.summary: The council moved the public comment period to a later point in the meeting.
8d133968ed8a08d2.impact: Residents who came to speak did so later in the evening. Nothing else changes.

8e0703e7da922819.headline: New rules for hiring a city manager
8e0703e7da922819.summary: The council took up a rewrite of the code covering its top staff job, renaming it 'city manager' and spelling out how a vacancy would be filled.
8e0703e7da922819.impact: This is internal government housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It only matters if the city's top administrator leaves: the council could name an interim and would interview at least three recruiting firms before choosing.

8e812934d688ef7c.headline: City hires a lobbyist for $60,000 a year
8e812934d688ef7c.summary: The city signed a one-year, $60,000 contract for lobbying services to represent Eagle Mountain's interests.
8e812934d688ef7c.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this is the city paying an outside firm to advocate for it, most likely at the state level.

8eda2d3a3da35661.headline: Mortgage help: city loans up to $25,000
8eda2d3a3da35661.summary: The city created a mortgage assistance program offering homebuyers loans of up to $25,000, prioritized by job type and then by lower household income.
8eda2d3a3da35661.impact: If you're buying a home in Eagle Mountain, you can apply for up to $25,000 toward the purchase. Households of six or more earning up to $151,800 may qualify, and an outside reviewer will check eligibility.

8efb0379a58bd336.headline: New historic zone created in city code
8efb0379a58bd336.summary: The council added a new "historic" zoning category to city code, striking one section (17.32.010(D)) from the version that was proposed.
8efb0379a58bd336.impact: No land was rezoned by this vote. But if your property is later placed in a historic zone, you would face extra rules on what you can build or change.

8f1c0ba0411f180f.headline: City code definitions amended
8f1c0ba0411f180f.summary: The council amended the definitions section of the city code, Section 17.10.030; the motion does not say which definitions changed.
8f1c0ba0411f180f.impact: The motion gives no detail on what was redefined, so there is nothing here that clearly changes anything for residents.

8f2ea24055e3e673.headline: Board appointment terms shift to an April start
8f2ea24055e3e673.summary: The city changed its code so library board and other appointments run April 1 through March 31 instead of the calendar year.
8f2ea24055e3e673.impact: This touches people who serve on city boards, not the public. If you sit on one, your term now starts in April rather than January.

8f8a3cb4ba0a391e.headline: City updates its building and construction standards
8f8a3cb4ba0a391e.summary: The council approved an updated Title 15, the city's building and construction standards and specifications, which now includes truck route approval requirements.
8f8a3cb4ba0a391e.impact: This is the technical rulebook builders and engineers follow. If you aren't building anything, nothing changes; if you are, your contractor works to the updated specs.

8f94fc7f68d413d2.headline: Residential development standards amended
8f94fc7f68d413d2.summary: The council approved an amendment to the city's residential development standards; the motion record does not state which requirement changed.
8f94fc7f68d413d2.impact: Nothing you'd notice day to day. The change applies to future home construction, and the motion itself doesn't say which standard was altered.

903efc4f2a54085b.headline: Impact fee cut for new businesses
903efc4f2a54085b.summary: The city partially suspended its transportation impact fee for nonresidential development, and dropped the carve-out that had applied to restaurants at every building size.
903efc4f2a54085b.impact: If you are building a business, store, or office in Eagle Mountain, you will pay less in road impact fees. The restaurant carve-out no longer applies at any size.

908e85a88dacf65d.headline: Arbor Day set for April 25
908e85a88dacf65d.summary: The council proclaimed April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day in Eagle Mountain.
908e85a88dacf65d.impact: Ceremonial only — nothing changes for residents. It's a symbolic nod to tree planting, with no new rules or spending attached.

90a1c2083f51a27d.headline: Create a Senior Citizens Advisory Board
90a1c2083f51a27d.summary: The city created a Senior Citizens Advisory Board by adding a new chapter to the municipal code.
90a1c2083f51a27d.impact: Nothing changes day to day. Older residents now have a formal board that can bring their concerns to the council; the seats are filled by separate appointments.

90d437975599839c.headline: Big Eagle 7 land rezoned for industrial use
90d437975599839c.summary: The council rezoned the land known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial zoning and applied an RTI overlay zone on top of it.
90d437975599839c.impact: This land is now set aside for industrial use rather than homes. If you live near Big Eagle 7, what gets built there in the future will be industrial.

90f4eb56507a2198.headline: Vote to deny the Harmony 14 subdivision plan
90f4eb56507a2198.summary: The council considered rejecting the preliminary plat — the proposed lot layout — for the Harmony 14 subdivision.
90f4eb56507a2198.impact: This is the step where the city signs off on how a subdivision is laid out, so it affects the Harmony 14 developer and anyone living near the site. The record here gives no reasons.

913e8b0a8982e106.headline: Steeplechase South subdivision plat amended
913e8b0a8982e106.summary: The city approved a second plat amendment for the Steeplechase South subdivision at 877 N Pony Express Parkway.
913e8b0a8982e106.impact: This adjusts the recorded layout of one subdivision on Pony Express Parkway. Unless you live in or are buying in Steeplechase South, nothing changes for you.

9199d4b0d3ed38e1.headline: Future land use map redrawn for master plan area
9199d4b0d3ed38e1.summary: The city redrew its long-range land use map for 27 parcels in the Eagle Mountain Properties area, designating large stretches as parks and open space, business park, and community commercial.
9199d4b0d3ed38e1.impact: This is the city's plan for what the land should eventually become, not a permit to build. It signals where future parks, shops, and business parks may go.

920a39d6593938ff.headline: Drinking water master plan and impact fee plan adopted
920a39d6593938ff.summary: The city adopted its long-range plan for drinking water facilities along with the impact fee plan that sets what new construction pays toward them.
920a39d6593938ff.impact: Nothing changes on your water bill today. The plan decides which water projects get built and is the basis for fees charged to new homes and buildings, not to existing ones.

933ecc894562afd9.headline: Chad Decoursey joins the Planning Commission
933ecc894562afd9.summary: The council appointed Chad Decoursey to fill a vacated Planning Commission seat, a roughly one-year term running from May 2026 through March 2027.
933ecc894562afd9.impact: Nothing changes for residents right away, though the Planning Commission is the board that reviews zoning and new development before it reaches the council.

93e5fc05941a0f2f.headline: Six wayfinding signs from Impact Signs
93e5fc05941a0f2f.summary: The council took up an agreement with Impact Signs to supply six wayfinding signs; the motion doesn't state a cost.
93e5fc05941a0f2f.impact: If it moves ahead, you'd see six new directional signs around the city. Nothing else changes.

94d77853e78b1388.headline: November named Hunger Awareness Month
94d77853e78b1388.summary: The council proclaimed November 2025 as Hunger Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
94d77853e78b1388.impact: This is a ceremonial statement — nothing changes for residents, and no money or city services are affected.

9592a88121c12468.headline: Shift road money to Mid Valley Road widening
9592a88121c12468.summary: The city amended its 2023-24 budget to move money set aside for Walden Park Road over to the Mid Valley Road widening project.
9592a88121c12468.impact: If you drive Mid Valley Road, this is the funding step that has to happen before widening work can go ahead. Nothing changes in what you pay.

96884106578745e6.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled
96884106578745e6.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling item 14.A. out for separate discussion and folding in a correction to the March 18 minutes.
96884106578745e6.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. This is the single batch vote the council uses to clear uncontested items at once.

97d87823c9cde42c.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
97d87823c9cde42c.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, moving the road-closure ordinance to full discussion and removing another item from the agenda entirely.
97d87823c9cde42c.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the procedural step that groups routine items into a single vote.

986d5d7fead215c5.headline: Storm water rules updated
986d5d7fead215c5.summary: The council amended the city's storm water ordinance, the rules covering runoff and drainage.
986d5d7fead215c5.impact: The motion doesn't say what changed, so it points to no specific effect on residents. Rules like these mainly govern builders and how new development handles runoff.

988a3cbedcd369fc.headline: Chad Decoursey named planning commission alternate
988a3cbedcd369fc.summary: The council appointed Chad Decoursey as an alternate on the planning commission for a three-year term running through December 2028.
988a3cbedcd369fc.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. An alternate fills in on the board that reviews zoning and development proposals when a regular member cannot attend.

98ab14e03fe7ad4a.headline: Consent agenda approved, three items pulled
98ab14e03fe7ad4a.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling two items for separate discussion and dropping a third from the agenda entirely.
98ab14e03fe7ad4a.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the procedural step that clears routine items in one vote and moves the rest into open discussion.

9a23406c979c5088.headline: Adam Jacobs joins the Library Advisory Board
9a23406c979c5088.summary: The council appointed Adam Jacobs to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board, running through 2027.
9a23406c979c5088.impact: Nothing changes for library users — this fills one volunteer seat on the board that advises the city on the library.

9a73c651d5e27bfb.headline: Firefly NPA 9.A site plan approved
9a73c651d5e27bfb.summary: The council approved the master site plan for Firefly NPA 9.A, the layout that governs how that part of the Firefly area gets built.
9a73c651d5e27bfb.impact: This clears the way for building in that section of Firefly. The motion does not state what is going in or how much, so the details sit in the site plan itself.

9ac9c33945e1ee9d.headline: Consent agenda approved
9ac9c33945e1ee9d.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items handled together without separate discussion.
9ac9c33945e1ee9d.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the routine step that clears grouped housekeeping items in one vote.

9bd684a3c75fc825.headline: Speed bumps added to council's study list
9bd684a3c75fc825.summary: The council added an evaluation of speed bumps and speed tables to its Legislative Priorities List.
9bd684a3c75fc825.impact: Nothing changes on your street. This only puts the question of speed bumps and speed tables on the council's list of things to look at later.

9c30a77b7d1340bf.headline: Rose Ranch subdivision agreement approved
9c30a77b7d1340bf.summary: The city approved a master development agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision, striking one water rights sentence and directing staff to keep negotiating a water delivery schedule.
9c30a77b7d1340bf.impact: Rose Ranch can now move ahead under an agreed set of terms, so expect building in that area. The water piece isn't settled — staff will keep negotiating when and how the developer turns over water.

9c673da62350dec7.headline: Legislative priorities list updated
9c673da62350dec7.summary: The council marked its review of conditional-use zoning rules as finished and dropped a neighborhood lot-size item it had already tabled.
9c673da62350dec7.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the council keeping its own to-do list current.

9cce80d294e470c0.headline: New park and city signs sent back to staff
9cce80d294e470c0.summary: The council rejected a contract with Identity Signs for six new wayfinding signs and told staff to find sturdier materials and cheaper installation.
9cce80d294e470c0.impact: The aging signs directing you to parks like Smith Ranch Park stay as they are for now, and new ones will not go up this fall as staff had hoped.

9d24930397b4852d.headline: Support America250 and a local anniversary group
9d24930397b4852d.summary: The city backed America250 Utah and formally recognized an Eagle Mountain committee to mark the nation's 250th anniversary.
9d24930397b4852d.impact: Nothing changes day to day. You may see the committee plan anniversary events, but the resolution itself is a statement of support and commits no money.

9d45f0489af82101.headline: New rules for closing roads during construction
9d45f0489af82101.summary: The city rewrote its road-closure rules, requiring contractors to submit a traffic control plan and a plan for notifying residents seven days before working in the street.
9d45f0489af82101.impact: If crews are about to tear up your street, they now need an approved plan for warning you first. Contractors must get a permit and give the city notice before any work starts.

9d9e3c20c4c640b0.headline: Bigger no-build buffer around natural washes
9d9e3c20c4c640b0.summary: The council took up a rule barring permanent buildings and earthwork within 75 feet of a wash's center flowline, or 50 feet from its bank, whichever is greater.
9d9e3c20c4c640b0.impact: If your lot backs onto a dry wash, this limits how close you can build or dig. It applies to homes, shops, and business parks alike, with the city engineer measuring the buffer.

9da027445fa014ee.headline: Enyo development agreement taken up
9da027445fa014ee.summary: The council considered an ordinance approving a development agreement with Enyo, as written in the meeting's agenda packet.
9da027445fa014ee.impact: A development agreement sets what a developer may build and what the city requires in return. The motion itself gives no location, size, or dollar figures, so the terms are only in the packet.

9da657a0a578c38f.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item held back
9da657a0a578c38f.summary: The council approved its consent agenda of grouped items, pulling item 10.A. out and setting it aside for later.
9da657a0a578c38f.impact: Nothing changes for residents — the consent agenda is the batch of uncontested items the council passes in a single vote.

9ea6ef667575e4a9.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
9ea6ef667575e4a9.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling items 12.A. and 13.A. out for separate discussion.
9ea6ef667575e4a9.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the routine step that passes uncontroversial items in one vote, with two set aside for their own debate.

9eb6b795dde6870c.headline: Change to the Eagle Quest East development deal
9eb6b795dde6870c.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the master development agreement covering the Eagle Quest East project.
9eb6b795dde6870c.impact: The motion does not spell out what changed. A master development agreement sets the ground rules for how a project area gets built, so this matters mainly to the developer and to people living near Eagle Quest East.

9ebff98d296b5fb7.headline: Create a new school district with two neighbor cities
9ebff98d296b5fb7.summary: The council approved an agreement with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield Town to create a new school district, and backed a separate district for five other cities.
9ebff98d296b5fb7.impact: If you have school-age kids, this is the paperwork that starts a district shared with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield Town. The motion doesn't say when it would take effect, so nothing changes for you yet.

a03274ba9d9098a6.headline: Library board seat for Marcia Vasquez
a03274ba9d9098a6.summary: The council took up appointing Marcia Vasquez as a library board advisor for a three-year term through December 2028; the record does not show the result.
a03274ba9d9098a6.impact: Nothing changes for residents either way — this is a volunteer advisory seat tied to the city library.

a1820ed606c35e63.headline: Four zoning code sections updated
a1820ed606c35e63.summary: The council amended four sections of the city's zoning code; the motion gives no detail on what the changes actually do.
a1820ed606c35e63.impact: We can't tell you what changed — the record names only section numbers. They sit in Title 17, the zoning rules that govern what can be built and where.

a1b98064873923a3.headline: Change the fee for site plan amendments
a1b98064873923a3.summary: The council amended the city fee schedule to change what it charges for site plan amendments; the motion does not state the new amount.
a1b98064873923a3.impact: This touches builders and businesses that want to change an already-approved site plan, not ordinary homeowners. The record does not say what the fee now costs.

a5a48ae00479ee2e.headline: Election results certified; RAP tax passes
a5a48ae00479ee2e.summary: The council certified the November 4 election, declaring Jared R. Gray mayor, Brett L. Wright and Craig Whiting councilmembers, and the RAP tax approved by voters.
a5a48ae00479ee2e.impact: Your new mayor and two councilmembers are now officially elected, and Proposition 8 — the RAP tax — is formally adopted because voters approved it.

a63c4185b40e9de3.headline: Consent agenda approved
a63c4185b40e9de3.summary: The council approved its consent agenda of grouped items, correcting a typo to read 2026-2027 and pulling one item out for separate discussion.
a63c4185b40e9de3.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It's the single batch vote that clears uncontested items in one go.

a63fb54cd106b0ee.headline: Agreement approved over the Overland area
a63fb54cd106b0ee.summary: The council approved a memorandum of agreement concerning Overland; the motion itself does not spell out the terms.
a63fb54cd106b0ee.impact: The record gives no detail on what the city agreed to, so no effect on residents can honestly be described. It was pulled off the consent agenda for separate discussion.

a7744473c3e867db.headline: Melissa Clark named mayor pro tem
a7744473c3e867db.summary: The council named Councilmember Melissa Clark mayor pro tem, the role that chairs meetings when the mayor is absent.
a7744473c3e867db.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the standing arrangement the council makes each year so someone can run a meeting the mayor misses.

a8258678df50b0fb.headline: Harmony development agreement amended
a8258678df50b0fb.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the development agreement covering the Harmony preliminary plat.
a8258678df50b0fb.impact: This changes the terms the Harmony developer must build to. The motion doesn't say what was changed, so it gives you nothing concrete about what will look different on the ground.

a845f0fcca8f59ae.headline: Buy 21 acres for a future civic campus
a845f0fcca8f59ae.summary: The council took up an agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to buy 20.99 acres for a future civic campus, with limits on commercial building size struck from the deal.
a845f0fcca8f59ae.impact: If the purchase goes through, the city would own land it intends to use for future public buildings. Nothing changes for you now — no buildings, timeline, or price are set in this item.

a894c46e45031baa.headline: Drive-thru lane rules put on hold
a894c46e45031baa.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's rules for drive-thru lanes.
a894c46e45031baa.impact: Nothing changes for residents or businesses — the existing drive-thru rules stay in place until the council takes the item back up.

a8d9dd8144a1e646.headline: Traffic calming added to priority list
a8d9dd8144a1e646.summary: The council added traffic calming and other traffic-related actions to the city's list of legislative priorities.
a8d9dd8144a1e646.impact: No speed bumps or new signs come from this on its own. It flags traffic as something the city wants to work on; any real change comes later.

a93f6785760ffee7.headline: New fence and buffer rules, and a way to force repairs
a93f6785760ffee7.summary: The council approved fencing and buffer standards, barring berms or hedges as substitutes for required fences, defining split-rail fencing, and letting the city treat unsafe fences as nuisances.
a93f6785760ffee7.impact: If your fence is falling apart, built from broken or flammable scrap, or put up to spite a neighbor, the city can now declare it a nuisance and make you fix it. Most homeowners are unaffected.

a97668bac4a23362.headline: Ranches land rezoned for shops and open space
a97668bac4a23362.summary: The council rezoned more than a dozen parcels in The Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties areas, most to commercial-neighborhood zoning, with some as agriculture, open space or foothill housing.
a97668bac4a23362.impact: If you live near these parcels in The Ranches, expect shops and commercial buildings on most of them rather than houses, with a few kept as farmland or open space.

a993efb75d6417ba.headline: Water rights rules for new development changed
a993efb75d6417ba.summary: The council amended the city code covering water rights and concept plans, adopting the changes discussed at the meeting.
a993efb75d6417ba.impact: This lands mainly on developers and landowners bringing new projects forward; what they must supply before approval is changing. Nothing changes for existing homes or your water bill.

aa01de8998e8ddcd.headline: 73 acres shift from business park to housing
aa01de8998e8ddcd.summary: The city changed its long-range land use map for 73.03 acres north of SR-73, south of 8000 North and west of Airport Road, from business park and light industry to foothill homes.
aa01de8998e8ddcd.impact: That 73-acre stretch near SR-73 and Airport Road is now planned for houses instead of offices, warehouses and light industry. If you live nearby, expect a residential neighborhood there rather than a jobs district.

aa4d9e1b4696f758.headline: Rezone the land known as QTS-SCL 2
aa4d9e1b4696f758.summary: The council approved a zoning change for the land known as QTS-SCL 2; the motion does not state the acreage or the new zoning.
aa4d9e1b4696f758.impact: The change resets what can legally be built on that property. The record here does not say where the land is or what the new zoning allows.

aba14ae8632717df.headline: Development deal with Mountainland Supply approved
aba14ae8632717df.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Mountainland Supply; the motion itself does not state the site, the size, or the terms.
aba14ae8632717df.impact: A development agreement locks in what a builder may do on a specific piece of land. The motion doesn't say where that land is or what is going up, so the details sit in the agreement itself.

abbe954fdc6aaba7.headline: Spring Run Plaza decision delayed
abbe954fdc6aaba7.summary: The council set aside the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza instead of voting it up or down.
abbe954fdc6aaba7.impact: If you live near the proposed Spring Run Plaza, nothing is settled — the plan and the zoning change are still open and can come back to the council later.

acf44b8ab1af5acf.headline: Small Business Saturday proclaimed for Nov. 30
acf44b8ab1af5acf.summary: The city proclaimed November 30, 2024 as Small Business Saturday in Eagle Mountain.
acf44b8ab1af5acf.impact: This is ceremonial — nothing changes for residents or businesses. It's an encouragement to shop locally that day, with no rules, money, or programs attached.

ad2587863af7fd33.headline: Joshua Biagio appointed to Library Advisory Board
ad2587863af7fd33.summary: The council appointed Joshua Biagio to the Library Advisory Board, finishing a term that runs through December 2025.
ad2587863af7fd33.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this fills an unexpired seat on a board that advises the city on the library.

adc35def3daa6406.headline: Zayo fiber franchise agreement put on hold
adc35def3daa6406.summary: The council delayed a decision on a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, LLC, holding the item over rather than voting it up or down.
adc35def3daa6406.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now. The agreement is on hold and would have to come back to the council before it could take effect.

ae31f3e2e7e8c582.headline: Youth Council rules rewritten
ae31f3e2e7e8c582.summary: The council rewrote the section of city code that sets up and governs the Youth Council, with revisions worked out earlier the same night.
ae31f3e2e7e8c582.impact: This touches only the teens who serve on the Youth Council and those applying to join. For everyone else it is internal housekeeping.

ae96096f30375cf4.headline: Downtown master plan adopted
ae96096f30375cf4.summary: The council adopted the Downtown Master Plan, the city's guiding blueprint for how its downtown area should be developed.
ae96096f30375cf4.impact: Nothing changes on the ground right away, but this is the document staff and the council will point to when future downtown building and zoning proposals come up.

afe724f7d5fcaf5e.headline: New rules for keeping animals on your property
afe724f7d5fcaf5e.summary: The city set standards for alternative animal management plans and tied the permit to the applicant, so it ends automatically when the property is sold.
afe724f7d5fcaf5e.impact: If you keep animals under one of these plans, the approval is yours, not your land's. It does not transfer to a buyer — when you sell, the new owner has to apply on their own.

afeddd01223f3dc8.headline: Changed water rights developers must hand over
afeddd01223f3dc8.summary: The city changed the rules for the water rights new residential developments must provide before they can build.
afeddd01223f3dc8.impact: This lands on developers bringing new homes to the city, and on how much water the city banks as it grows. The motion doesn't spell out whether the requirement went up or down.

b010fc762d6bd6e5.headline: New sign rules for data center projects
b010fc762d6bd6e5.summary: The city changed its sign code to set rules for directional signage tied to data centers and other large-scale development projects.
b010fc762d6bd6e5.impact: You may see new directional signs around large development and data center sites. Nothing changes for ordinary homeowners or their own signs.

b02d2399f7d13e06.headline: Shared parking requirement lowered to 35%
b02d2399f7d13e06.summary: The council changed the rules on where parking areas can go and cut the required shared parking from 40% to 35%.
b02d2399f7d13e06.impact: This mainly touches developers and businesses building new commercial projects, which can now share slightly less of their parking. You may see lots laid out differently in future developments.

b04367e7c0e189e0.headline: Crosswalk deal at Woodhaven and Pony Express
b04367e7c0e189e0.summary: The city approved a reimbursement agreement for crosswalk access at Woodhaven Boulevard and Pony Express Parkway and directed staff to address unsafe winter conditions there.
b04367e7c0e189e0.impact: If you cross Pony Express Parkway at Woodhaven on foot, this covers the cost of crosswalk access at that corner, and city staff have been told to deal with what makes it dangerous in winter.

b0521f08c374d170.headline: Outside firm hired to run C-PACE projects
b0521f08c374d170.summary: The city hired Sustainable Real Estate Solutions to provide administrative and professional services for its C-PACE projects.
b0521f08c374d170.impact: Nothing changes day to day for residents — this hands the paperwork for C-PACE projects to an outside firm. The motion doesn't say what the city will pay for the service.

b0785b5369cc6956.headline: Youth Council rules rewritten
b0785b5369cc6956.summary: The council rewrote the rules for the city's Youth Council, moving the power to appoint youth members from the city manager to a committee of advisors.
b0785b5369cc6956.impact: This affects the teens who serve on the Youth Council and the adults who run it. Nothing changes for other residents.

b0a5aad17b6718e2.headline: Discount on a rezone fee turned down
b0a5aad17b6718e2.summary: The council declined Steve McCleery's request to cut the fee for his rezone application from $1,350 to $760.
b0a5aad17b6718e2.impact: Only the applicant is affected — he pays the full $1,350. The city's rezone application fee is unchanged for everyone else.

b16156fdb7ced2b2.headline: Updated transportation impact fee adopted
b16156fdb7ced2b2.summary: The city adopted an updated transportation impact fee, the charge new development pays toward roads, plus rules for collecting, appealing, and accounting for it.
b16156fdb7ced2b2.impact: This is paid by builders on new construction, not by homes already standing, so nothing changes on your bill. The motion does not state the new fee amount.

b23b3f296f36ccb8.headline: UTA park-and-ride site plan approved
b23b3f296f36ccb8.summary: The council approved the site plan for a UTA park-and-ride lot in Eagle Mountain.
b23b3f296f36ccb8.impact: The transit agency can move ahead with a lot where you would park and catch a bus. The motion gives no location, size, or opening date.

b2fcebc6a52f94cd.headline: Consent agenda approved
b2fcebc6a52f94cd.summary: The council passed its consent agenda as a single batch; the record does not list which items were included.
b2fcebc6a52f94cd.impact: Consent items are the routine business the council approves together without separate debate. The record here doesn't say what was in this batch.

b3611653e5b6e9e0.headline: Changes to the city zoning code adopted
b3611653e5b6e9e0.summary: The council amended Title 17, the city's zoning code, adopting the updated version included in the meeting packet.
b3611653e5b6e9e0.impact: Zoning rules govern what can be built on a property and where. The motion itself doesn't spell out what changed, so the effect on any given property isn't clear from the record.

b72f2754e043b54c.headline: City hires marketing firm at $3,500 a month
b72f2754e043b54c.summary: The city hired REDKOR Brand Campaigns to build a city marketing plan for $3,500 a month, cancellable at any time and capped at 14 months.
b72f2754e043b54c.impact: Nothing changes day to day. Over time you may notice more consistent city messaging about tourism and business, and the city can end the contract whenever it wants.

b8114e775c3829bf.headline: City joins Utah Valley HOME Consortium
b8114e775c3829bf.summary: Eagle Mountain agreed to join the Utah Valley HOME Consortium by signing a cooperation agreement with other local governments.
b8114e775c3829bf.impact: Nothing changes day to day. This is the paperwork that puts Eagle Mountain into a regional partnership with neighboring governments; the motion itself commits no money and starts no program.

ba151c1cad32d50a.headline: Mayor's powers item pushed later in the meeting
ba151c1cad32d50a.summary: The council set aside the mayor's powers ordinance until later in the same meeting so the public could comment on it first.
ba151c1cad32d50a.impact: This is a scheduling step — it gave residents a chance to speak before the council took the item up. Nothing changes for you.

ba8390ec229dbea0.headline: Motion to delay the land decision withdrawn
ba8390ec229dbea0.summary: A move to postpone the same land decision, with direction to work out a better solution with neighboring owners and city staff, was withdrawn.
ba8390ec229dbea0.impact: Nothing was decided here — the motion was taken back before any vote, so it changes nothing for residents.

bb0ce9a5a41a5692.headline: Rewrite of city governance rules put on hold
bb0ce9a5a41a5692.summary: The council delayed a decision on rewriting Title 2 of the city code, the section covering how city government itself operates.
bb0ce9a5a41a5692.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now. The rules governing how the city runs stay as they are until the council takes the item back up.

bbd70251fb86c33b.headline: City land to be sold at $95,000 an acre
bbd70251fb86c33b.summary: The council authorized selling a significant piece of city-owned property at a price of $95,000 per acre, or $2.18 per square foot.
bbd70251fb86c33b.impact: The motion doesn't name the parcel or the buyer; what it settles is the price the city will accept for land the public currently owns. Nothing changes day to day for residents.

bccbcc538a26dafa.headline: Approve Spring Run Plaza plan and rezone
bccbcc538a26dafa.summary: The council approved the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza, with the land under Roads A and B zoned Agriculture.
bccbcc538a26dafa.impact: This is the approval that lets Spring Run Plaza move forward, so neighbors can expect the project to proceed. The motion doesn't state its size, its uses, or a timeline.

bcf8d65a8fb69c43.headline: Consent agenda approved
bcf8d65a8fb69c43.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling the WDG website change order out of the batch for separate discussion.
bcf8d65a8fb69c43.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the routine step that passes uncontested items in a single vote.

beefc035773e3fc5.headline: Longer construction hours OK'd for QTS data center
beefc035773e3fc5.summary: The city let the QTS SLC1 data center site run construction outside the hours normally allowed under city code.
beefc035773e3fc5.impact: If you live near the QTS SLC1 site, construction noise may continue outside the usual permitted hours. The motion does not say which hours were granted or how long the exception lasts.

bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.headline: City to sell land at $2.07 a square foot
bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.summary: The council approved selling part of a city-owned parcel at $2.07 per square foot, with the total set by the final survey.
bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.impact: This is a one-off sale of city land and changes nothing at your home. Existing utility easements on the property stay in place, so the lines running through it are protected.

c0a3d421506c569d.headline: Transportation Master Plan put on hold
c0a3d421506c569d.summary: The council delayed adopting the Transportation Master Plan, the city's long-range plan for its road network.
c0a3d421506c569d.impact: No road decisions are locked in by this. The plan shapes where future roads and improvements go, and it has to come back to the council before it takes effect.

c11d4924ea69b4d3.headline: Add transit grant study to state lobbying list
c11d4924ea69b4d3.summary: The council added a study of public transit innovation grants to the list of priorities it takes to the state legislature.
c11d4924ea69b4d3.impact: Nothing changes for you now — this only signals what the city plans to ask state lawmakers about. Any actual transit service would need separate decisions later.

c1396eb7dc0a7c09.headline: Susan Allen joins the Senior Advisory Board
c1396eb7dc0a7c09.summary: The council appointed Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board for a term running through December 31, 2025.
c1396eb7dc0a7c09.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a seat on a volunteer advisory board through the end of the year.

c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.headline: Consent items approved with changes
c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after narrowing how sponsorship money may be spent, updating the city fee schedule, and setting a Youth City Council quorum.
c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.impact: Mostly housekeeping. The one piece that could reach you is the updated fee schedule, but the motion doesn't say which fees changed or by how much.

c2ef848260675e4a.headline: Youth Council rules adopted with mayor voting
c2ef848260675e4a.summary: With the mayor included in the vote, the council adopted the rewritten Youth Council rules, shifting appointment of youth members to a committee of advisors.
c2ef848260675e4a.impact: This affects the teens on the Youth Council and how they are chosen. Nothing changes for other residents.

c470bac794255243.headline: Temporary business signs added to lobbying list
c470bac794255243.summary: The council added a temporary business signage provision to its Legislative Priorities List and directed staff to come back with a proposal.
c470bac794255243.impact: Nothing changes yet for businesses or sign rules — this only puts the topic on the city's priority list and starts staff working on a proposal.

c4c04b5288e2025b.headline: September named PTA Membership Month
c4c04b5288e2025b.summary: The city proclaimed September 2024 as Parent Teacher Association Membership Month.
c4c04b5288e2025b.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a ceremonial recognition of local PTA volunteers, with no cost or requirement attached.

c5a5d089d8c23823.headline: Josh Biagio appointed to library board
c5a5d089d8c23823.summary: The council appointed Josh Biagio to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board, from January 2026 through December 2028.
c5a5d089d8c23823.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer seat on the board that advises the city on the library.

c6f877e1c66027af.headline: Rodeo and demolition derby join Pony Express Days
c6f877e1c66027af.summary: The council formally recognized the PRCA rodeo and the demolition derby as official events of the city's Pony Express Days celebration.
c6f877e1c66027af.impact: Nothing changes day to day for residents — this is a formal blessing that lets the rodeo and derby run under the city's Pony Express Days banner.

c7473d91a4f0fefa.headline: Eagle Square commercial development approved
c7473d91a4f0fefa.summary: The council approved the preliminary layout for the Eagle Square commercial development, requiring the traffic study be used to place its entrance off Pony Express Parkway.
c7473d91a4f0fefa.impact: A commercial development moves ahead on Pony Express Parkway. Its south entrance must be sited using the traffic study so it lines up with the intersection to the south.

c832a74e1f6d3f2d.headline: Two items pulled for separate discussion
c832a74e1f6d3f2d.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled the civic campus land purchase and the lobbying contract out for individual discussion.
c832a74e1f6d3f2d.impact: This is procedural housekeeping — it only means two items got their own debate instead of passing in a batch.

ca8575974ec16800.headline: March named MS Awareness Month
ca8575974ec16800.summary: The council proclaimed March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
ca8575974ec16800.impact: This is a ceremonial statement — nothing changes for residents, and no city money or rules are involved.

cb37ab239acc9a49.headline: City won't sell off a piece of its land
cb37ab239acc9a49.summary: The council rejected a proposal to dispose of part of a city-owned parcel that the city code treats as significant real property.
cb37ab239acc9a49.impact: The land stays in city hands and nothing changes on the ground. The request to take over part of the parcel was turned down.

cbbf7bad913e0758.headline: Consent items approved, with school traffic conditions
cbbf7bad913e0758.summary: The council approved its consent agenda and attached staff conditions requiring intersection improvements to the John Hancock Charter School west campus item.
cbbf7bad913e0758.impact: Mostly routine housekeeping. The one piece with teeth is that the charter school's west campus must meet the city's conditions on intersection improvements, which matters to people driving near that site.

cbd16e2de476bfa3.headline: New easement rules added to the land use code
cbd16e2de476bfa3.summary: The city added a new easements chapter to its land use code and updated the code's definitions to match.
cbd16e2de476bfa3.impact: This mainly touches property owners and developers dealing with easements — the strips of land set aside for things like utilities or access. Most residents will see no change day to day.

cc05b380718811e6.headline: Consent agenda and 2025 meeting dates
cc05b380718811e6.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulled two items out for separate discussion, and added November 5 and December 16 to the 2025 meeting calendar.
cc05b380718811e6.impact: Nothing changes for residents beyond two extra council meetings on next year's calendar — this is the routine batch approval of uncontested items.

ccca5fa20a6b8eb8.headline: Draft budget opens for public comment June 3
ccca5fa20a6b8eb8.summary: The council adopted a tentative budget for the 2025-2026 budget year and set a public hearing on the final version for June 3, 2025.
ccca5fa20a6b8eb8.impact: Nothing changes yet — this is the step that puts next year's spending plan on the table for public review. If you want a say in it, the hearing is June 3.

cd7f19a7f28a7115.headline: Screening rules for apartment buildings delayed
cd7f19a7f28a7115.summary: The council delayed a decision on rules for screening heat pumps and other equipment on apartment buildings, sending it back for revisions.
cd7f19a7f28a7115.impact: Nothing changes right now. The rewritten rules will come back to the council later, and they mainly affect apartment builders rather than homeowners.

ce234a07251ede47.headline: Add concrete form pricing to the priorities list
ce234a07251ede47.summary: The council added the pricing of concrete forms to the city's legislative priorities list for staff to look into.
ce234a07251ede47.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this just flags a topic for future discussion, with no decision or cost attached to it yet.

ce8dca0a1cf4a8c5.headline: Mid-year budget changes approved
ce8dca0a1cf4a8c5.summary: The council approved the second set of changes to the city's 2024-2025 budget; the record doesn't say which line items changed.
ce8dca0a1cf4a8c5.impact: The record doesn't spell out what changed, so there's no stated effect on your taxes, fees or services — the details sit in the city's budget amendment documents.

cf3d08f7ba130b39.headline: City to sell a small parcel to adjoining owners
cf3d08f7ba130b39.summary: The city approved selling 0.156 acres of city-owned land to the owners of the neighboring lots, with the sale to be finished by February 19, 2026.
cf3d08f7ba130b39.impact: Only the owners of the adjoining lots are affected. They can buy the parcels together on one application, and within six months their fences must sit on the correct lot line or be removed.

cfb2c650bc0473a5.headline: Consent items approved, mortgage contract flagged
cfb2c650bc0473a5.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling the credit card policy out and requiring the mortgage assistance contract to return to council if applications exceed 100.
cfb2c650bc0473a5.impact: Nothing changes day to day. If the city's mortgage assistance program draws more than 100 loan applications, the contract with its administrator comes back to the council for another look.

cfdb11c54689274c.headline: Land swap with the state in the Overland area
cfdb11c54689274c.summary: The city approved trading properties with the state trust lands agency (SITLA) in the Overland area, conditioned on matching contract language and a clean title guarantee.
cfdb11c54689274c.impact: It reshuffles which parcels the city and the state each own out in the Overland area. Nothing changes at your home now, but it shapes what the city can do with that land later.

d0aa16b3e51f4296.headline: Meeting capped at 11 p.m.
d0aa16b3e51f4296.summary: The council agreed to end the night's meeting at 11:00 p.m.
d0aa16b3e51f4296.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is housekeeping the council uses to limit how late the meeting runs.

d0aeca50b71295f6.headline: Decision delayed on alternative energy zone rules
d0aeca50b71295f6.summary: The council delayed a decision on creating a new Alternative Energy Overlay Zone in the city code.
d0aeca50b71295f6.impact: No rules changed. The proposal comes back to the council another day, so there is still time to weigh in before anything is decided.

d1dc76a647463d18.headline: Development deal for Harmony Subdivision homes
d1dc76a647463d18.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Meritage Homes setting the terms for the Harmony Subdivision.
d1dc76a647463d18.impact: This locks in the rules Meritage Homes must build to at Harmony. The motion itself doesn't state how many homes, what they cost, or when building starts, so there is nothing yet for neighbors to plan around.

d28d136d84e6d999.headline: Liquor license rules updated
d28d136d84e6d999.summary: The council approved an update to the city's liquor licensing rules; the motion record does not spell out what changed.
d28d136d84e6d999.impact: This touches businesses that sell alcohol, not most residents. Because the motion doesn't state the change, check the ordinance text itself if you hold or want a liquor license.

d3248c1d81e909c6.headline: Susan Allen appointed senior advisor
d3248c1d81e909c6.summary: The council signed off on appointing Susan Allen as senior advisor for a three-year term running January 2026 through December 2028.
d3248c1d81e909c6.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a routine appointment to an advisory role.

d34546e2ecdb529b.headline: Lower $45,000-an-acre price rejected
d34546e2ecdb529b.summary: The council rejected a lower price of $45,000 per acre ($1.03 per square foot) for the same city land, on the argument that the parcel needs no added water rights.
d34546e2ecdb529b.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this was a competing price for the same parcel, and the higher price the council approved is what stands.

d379492c19d866fb.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 rezoned to RC
d379492c19d866fb.summary: The council changed the zoning on the Cedar Corners Phase 5 land from residential to the city's RC zone.
d379492c19d866fb.impact: This is the zoning step behind the Cedar Corners Phase 5 project. If you live nearby, what can be built on that land is now governed by RC zone rules instead of the old residential rules.

d420c4bcf28a2417.headline: Sales tax pledged to back redevelopment bonds
d420c4bcf28a2417.summary: The council took up a resolution pledging part of the city's sales tax revenue to repay bonds the city's redevelopment agency plans to issue in 2026.
d420c4bcf28a2417.impact: No new tax and no bill for you. The city would be promising some of its sales tax income to bondholders, money that would otherwise be free for other city spending.

d4c1e66118361b7f.headline: Sale of small city parcel delayed
d4c1e66118361b7f.summary: The council delayed a decision on selling a 0.156-acre piece of city property, and on the terms of that sale.
d4c1e66118361b7f.impact: Nothing changes for residents — the city holds onto the parcel until the council revisits the sale.

d5db525af3de6295.headline: Industrial zone rules replaced; farm zone tweaked
d5db525af3de6295.summary: The city replaced its industrial zone rules and adjusted the agriculture and commercial storage zones, requiring special approval for equestrian centers and capping moving vehicles at six.
d5db525af3de6295.impact: If you run or plan an equestrian center, a storage yard, or an industrial business, the rules for what you can build and how many trucks you can keep on site have changed. Most residents will notice nothing.

d61cfe930fa6a402.headline: Consent agenda approved, with items set aside
d61cfe930fa6a402.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling items 10.A, 10.B and 12.A for separate votes, moving item 13.A to full discussion, and fixing spelling in 13.B.
d61cfe930fa6a402.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It is how the council passes uncontroversial items in one batch while separating out the ones it wants to handle on their own.

d637bf8739c91d41.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook land rezoned for homes
d637bf8739c91d41.summary: The city rezoned the Cedar Valley Holbrook property from agriculture to foothill residential, on the condition that wildlife corridor fencing be marked on the west side.
d637bf8739c91d41.impact: Land that could only be farmed can now be built with homes. Neighbors will eventually see houses where open agricultural ground is today, with fencing marking the wildlife corridor along the west edge.

d6fa117bfdadac7e.headline: Council board assignments put on hold
d6fa117bfdadac7e.summary: The council kept its 2024 board liaison assignments until the mayor can meet with members to set new ones, and asked staff for a list of all boards.
d6fa117bfdadac7e.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is internal housekeeping about which councilmember sits in on which city board and commission.

d79e0336ab37cba8.headline: Employee credit card policy put on hold
d79e0336ab37cba8.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's employee credit card policy and sent it back for more discussion in a work session.
d79e0336ab37cba8.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is an internal rule about how city staff spend on city cards, and the council wants another look before voting.

d79e889cb4d263f6.headline: Possible parks and arts sales tax on 2025 ballot
d79e889cb4d263f6.summary: The council took up a proposal to have staff study placing a Recreation, Arts and Parks (RAP) sales tax question on the 2025 city election ballot.
d79e889cb4d263f6.impact: Nothing changes now — this is only analysis. If the council later moves ahead, you would get the final say on the tax at the 2025 municipal election.

d7e0a3a2f87ca7f2.headline: Verizon cell tower site plan approved
d7e0a3a2f87ca7f2.summary: The city approved the site plan for a Verizon communications tower.
d7e0a3a2f87ca7f2.impact: If you live near the site, a new tower is cleared to go up. The motion doesn't say where in the city it will stand.

d832e11d06d2a6ed.headline: Move to reject Hidden Hollow amenity swap
d832e11d06d2a6ed.summary: The council took up a proposal to reject the Hidden Hollow amenity change outright rather than leave it for a later meeting.
d832e11d06d2a6ed.impact: Nothing is settled for Hidden Hollow either way — the amenity change was neither approved nor finally rejected at this meeting.

d8e4e31bf7ee8eaf.headline: City map redrawn for future shops and parks
d8e4e31bf7ee8eaf.summary: The council redrew its long-range land use map for certain Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties parcels, marking most for community commercial and several for parks and open space.
d8e4e31bf7ee8eaf.impact: This is the planning step that lines the city's official map up with the zoning change on those same parcels. For neighbors, it points to shops, parks and open space instead of more housing.

d929de26b7bec679.headline: Pay schedule for city officers updated
d929de26b7bec679.summary: The council amended the compensation schedule for the city's statutory officers.
d929de26b7bec679.impact: This sets what the city's statutory officers are paid. The motion does not state the new figures, and nothing changes for residents day to day.

d9d471ec3aae5e3f.headline: Consent agenda approved, manager contract pulled
d9d471ec3aae5e3f.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, but pulled out the interim city manager agreement with Stephen Mumford and shortened a legislative consulting renewal to two years.
d9d471ec3aae5e3f.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. The interim city manager contract was set aside to be handled separately.

d9fea19b0652cb03.headline: Mayor and council pay raised, starting January
d9fea19b0652cb03.summary: The city set the mayor's pay at $119,800 plus a $600 monthly car allowance and council pay at $18,100 a year, effective January 1, 2025.
d9fea19b0652cb03.impact: This is taxpayer money going to the city's elected officials. The new amounts take effect January 1, 2025; there is no direct change to your bills or services.

da91557fd8eb9772.headline: City's legislative wish list, plus a grant program
da91557fd8eb9772.summary: The council took up its list of priorities to push at the Utah Legislature, adding a matching-grant program for future consideration.
da91557fd8eb9772.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day — this is the city deciding what to ask state lawmakers for. Any real effect would depend on what the Legislature does later.

dac95bfa458a71ca.headline: City fee schedule updated
dac95bfa458a71ca.summary: The council approved changes to the city's consolidated fee schedule, the master list of what people pay for permits, licenses and city services.
dac95bfa458a71ca.impact: If you pull a permit or pay for a city service, the price may have changed. The motion itself doesn't say which fees moved or by how much.

dad3a2517f272def.headline: Ask lawmakers to open mortgage aid to veterans
dad3a2517f272def.summary: The council put expanding the mortgage assistance program to veterans, active-duty military, and public servants on its list of state legislative priorities.
dad3a2517f272def.impact: Nothing changes yet — this only tells state lawmakers what Eagle Mountain wants. Any actual home-buying help for veterans and military families would have to come from the Legislature.

db9159fdf786a630.headline: Parkway Fields plan reshuffled, no added homes
db9159fdf786a630.summary: The council approved a revised Parkway Fields plan: re-phased townhomes, a small strip rezoned for about four extra townhomes offset by fewer lots elsewhere, and no density increase.
db9159fdf786a630.impact: If you live in or are buying in Parkway Fields, phase labels and the street layout change, and the developer dedicates land for Old Airport Road plus open space with a trail and trailhead. Total home count stays flat.

dbb70ee232fb274a.headline: Push to reject the HOME Consortium deal
dbb70ee232fb274a.summary: The council did not take up a proposal to reject the Utah Valley HOME Consortium agreement, which it approved on a separate motion.
dbb70ee232fb274a.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this was an attempt to turn down the consortium agreement rather than sign it, and it went no further.

dcb2b6dd0dbc4c15.headline: Updated water conservation plan adopted
dcb2b6dd0dbc4c15.summary: The city adopted an amended water conservation and management plan, the document that sets out how Eagle Mountain manages and conserves its water supply.
dcb2b6dd0dbc4c15.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this adopts a planning document. The council did not set any new watering rules or restrictions with this vote.

deb37438d3401890.headline: Draft 2026-27 budget accepted, hearings set
deb37438d3401890.summary: The council accepted the tentative city budget for 2026–2027 and set public hearings for June 16, 2026 and August 18, 2026.
deb37438d3401890.impact: No money is locked in yet. If you want a say in how the city spends next year, those two hearing dates are when to show up.

df5c12ce72c47325.headline: Sewer plant to use membrane treatment technology
df5c12ce72c47325.summary: The city settled on membrane bioreactor (MBR) treatment technology and a construction-manager delivery method for its proposed new sewer treatment plant.
df5c12ce72c47325.impact: This locks in how the planned sewer plant will clean wastewater and how it gets built. Nothing changes on your bill today — the motion names no cost or timeline.

dfa6b60515fc7bbb.headline: Interim budget and proposed tax rate adopted
dfa6b60515fc7bbb.summary: The council adopted an interim budget for the 2026-2027 fiscal year and the proposed certified tax rate, and dropped the city's DebtBook software service.
dfa6b60515fc7bbb.impact: This keeps the city funded until a final budget is adopted and sets the property tax rate the city is proposing. The motion states no dollar figures.

e0bebb6adf467ca1.headline: Hotel height and parking rules put on hold
e0bebb6adf467ca1.summary: The council delayed easing the height limit and parking requirements for hotels until the city's hotel feasibility study is finished.
e0bebb6adf467ca1.impact: No hotel is approved or blocked by this. The rules a would-be hotel developer said were in the way stay as they are until the study comes back.

e135c6867636244a.headline: Recruiting consultants contract put on hold
e135c6867636244a.summary: The council delayed a decision on a professional services contract with recruitment consultants Jason Walker and David Kitchen.
e135c6867636244a.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a staffing contract the council chose to look at again later.

e176e09fe57af0ea.headline: Public art plan adopted
e176e09fe57af0ea.summary: The city adopted a Public Art Plan to guide how Eagle Mountain approaches art in public places.
e176e09fe57af0ea.impact: Nothing changes day to day. The plan sets the city's general approach; any specific artwork or spending would still need its own approval.

e1809490a455a781.headline: Routine items approved, four pulled off the list
e1809490a455a781.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling three items out for full discussion and dropping a fourth item from the agenda entirely.
e1809490a455a781.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the housekeeping step that clears uncontroversial items in a single vote. The three pulled items were debated separately later in the meeting.

e18a3fbe3d10b9eb.headline: Fees changed for sewer, storm water, and building
e18a3fbe3d10b9eb.summary: The city amended its fee schedule, changing code enforcement fines, building department fees, sewer rates, and storm water charges.
e18a3fbe3d10b9eb.impact: Sewer and storm water charges are part of your city utility bill, so this reaches every household; the building and enforcement changes hit anyone pulling a permit or cited for a violation. The motion doesn't state the new amounts.

e1dd54be7a8a0438.headline: Parkway Fields development agreement amended
e1dd54be7a8a0438.summary: The council approved an amendment to the Parkway Fields (Ault Farms) master development agreement, the contract setting the terms the developer must build to.
e1dd54be7a8a0438.impact: This matters mainly if you live in or near Parkway Fields. It updates the developer's obligations for that project; nothing changes elsewhere in the city.

e3aae1156fe3f502.headline: Primary results certified; November ballot set
e3aae1156fe3f502.summary: The city certified the August 12 primary, in which 6,866 of 26,930 mailed ballots came back, and named the six candidates advancing to the November 4 election.
e3aae1156fe3f502.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this makes the primary official. Your November 4 ballot will list Melissa Clark and Jared Gray for mayor, and Emily Buss, Brett Wright, Craig Whiting, and Charlotte Ducos for council.

e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.headline: Ask the state to fund a sidewalk near Walmart
e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.summary: The council added construction of a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near Walmart to the list of priorities it takes to state lawmakers.
e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.impact: Nothing is built or funded yet — this only puts the sidewalk on the city's ask list. If the state pays for it, people walking near Walmart get a sidewalk.

e42b3fd490442908.headline: Decision delayed on required mix of lot sizes
e42b3fd490442908.summary: The council delayed a decision on a new rule that would require a mixture of lot sizes in developments.
e42b3fd490442908.impact: Nothing changes for now. The rule would apply to developers laying out new subdivisions, not to existing homeowners, and it comes back to the council later.

e44be31c3f0bb8af.headline: Mid-year budget change for 2023-24
e44be31c3f0bb8af.summary: The council adopted the third amendment to the city's 2023-24 budget; the motion does not say which line items changed.
e44be31c3f0bb8af.impact: This is routine bookkeeping — the city adjusts its budget mid-year as costs and revenues shift. Nothing changes for you day to day, and the record gives no detail on what moved.

e461251be4e585cf.headline: Mayor can't create city policy without a council vote
e461251be4e585cf.summary: The council adopted rules barring the mayor or staff from enacting policy without a majority council vote, and requiring the council to vote on liaison assignments.
e461251be4e585cf.impact: This is about who holds power inside city hall, not your street or your bill. New city rules now have to clear a council vote in a public meeting rather than being set by the mayor's office.

e48e947a787617a3.headline: Bryan Free added as planning commission alternate
