e48e947a787617a3.summary: The council appointed Bryan Free as an alternate on the planning commission, finishing a two-year term that runs through December 2025.
e48e947a787617a3.impact: Nothing changes for you now. He steps in when a regular commissioner is absent from the board that reviews zoning and development plans.

e4e946b31067d6d2.headline: Jared Gray named mayor pro tem
e4e946b31067d6d2.summary: The council elected Councilmember Jared Gray as mayor pro tempore, the member who fills in when the mayor is unavailable.
e4e946b31067d6d2.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is internal housekeeping about who steps in to run a meeting when the mayor can't be there.

e5fa836dc05db55d.headline: 672-acre development deal near the data centers
e5fa836dc05db55d.summary: The council took up a development agreement covering about 672 acres on two parcels, one near the Meta, Google, and QTS sites and one beside the Firefly area.
e5fa836dc05db55d.impact: This touches landowners and neighbors near the data center campuses and in the southwest near Firefly. The council rewrote the buffering language so it only binds land once that land is annexed into the city.

e6121ee0b6b74fcb.headline: Study a policy on paper water rights
e6121ee0b6b74fcb.summary: The council directed staff to work with them on a policy covering paper water rights and priority dates, adding it to the city's legislative priorities list.
e6121ee0b6b74fcb.impact: Nothing changes yet — this only puts the topic on the city's to-do list. Any actual water rights policy would have to come back to the council later.

e720a89cb623a7a3.headline: Land use map updated for Cedar Corners Phase 5
e720a89cb623a7a3.summary: The council changed the city's long-range land use map for Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Neighborhood Residential 1 to Neighborhood Residential 2.
e720a89cb623a7a3.impact: This updates the city's long-term plan for that land so it matches the rezoning approved the same night. Nothing changes anywhere else in the city.

e854f84a97214b26.headline: Updated city water conservation plan
e854f84a97214b26.summary: The council adopted an amended water conservation and management plan, the city's blueprint for how it saves and manages its water supply.
e854f84a97214b26.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day — this updates a planning document. The motion sets no new watering rules or rates.

e8a7409ac69f7fc7.headline: Up to $230M in water and sewer bonds
e8a7409ac69f7fc7.summary: The council authorized borrowing up to $230 million by issuing water and sewer revenue bonds, and set the maximum term, interest rate, and discount for the sale.
e8a7409ac69f7fc7.impact: Revenue bonds are repaid from what the city collects on water and sewer bills rather than from property taxes, so ratepayers ultimately carry this debt. A public hearing is required before the bonds are sold.

e9575ce1c444c10d.headline: Design rules updated for shops and apartments
e9575ce1c444c10d.summary: The council updated the city's design standards for commercial buildings and apartments, changing how new projects of that kind must be built and look.
e9575ce1c444c10d.impact: Nothing changes for existing homes. The new standards shape the appearance of stores and apartment buildings approved from here on, and developers will have to design to them.

e9b96549abc6dcf6.headline: Stricter rules for steel fences
e9b96549abc6dcf6.summary: The city set new standards for steel fencing, requiring weathering steel at least 1/8 inch thick, banning corrugated panels, and dropping the annual sealing rule.
e9b96549abc6dcf6.impact: If you put up a steel fence, the city will now check the metal's thickness when you pull your permit, corrugated panels are no longer allowed, and you no longer have to seal it every year.

eb3ae48f03a35267.headline: Dillon Boss appointed to the library board
eb3ae48f03a35267.summary: The council appointed Dillon Boss to the Library Advisory Board for a one-year term through December 2024.
eb3ae48f03a35267.impact: Nothing changes at the library — this is a volunteer advisory seat being filled.

eb888342c0eab8c1.headline: Mary Hammond joins senior advisory council
eb888342c0eab8c1.summary: The council appointed Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, completing a four-year term that runs through 2025.
eb888342c0eab8c1.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a volunteer seat on the board that advises the city on issues affecting seniors.

ec49bd5e3e123e43.headline: Development agreement with Meta approved
ec49bd5e3e123e43.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Stadion, LLC — the company known as Meta — setting the terms for its Eagle Mountain project.
ec49bd5e3e123e43.impact: This sets the ground rules for what Meta may build here and what it owes the city. The motion doesn't list those terms, so residents won't see anything change day to day.

ec5654790d88548e.headline: New rules for fences and privacy screening
ec5654790d88548e.summary: The city amended its code covering fences, privacy screening, and the table of land uses allowed in each zone; the motion does not state what specifically changed.
ec5654790d88548e.impact: If you are planning a fence or a screening wall on your property, the rules you have to build to have changed — check the current code before you start.

ed21c804323e671e.headline: Laura Jensen named Planning Commission alternate
ed21c804323e671e.summary: The council appointed Laura Jensen as an alternate on the Planning Commission for a three-year term running from May 2026 to March 2029.
ed21c804323e671e.impact: Nothing changes day to day. Alternates step in when a regular commissioner is absent from the board that reviews zoning and development proposals.

ed5174ede43e72a8.headline: Franchise deal approved with SummitIG Fiber
ed5174ede43e72a8.summary: The city approved a franchise agreement with SummitIG Fiber, LLC, the standard permission a fiber-optic company needs to do business in Eagle Mountain.
ed5174ede43e72a8.impact: Nothing changes for you today. The motion does not say what SummitIG will build, where, or when — only that the company now has a franchise agreement with the city.

ed82aab2c197cf10.headline: 2025-26 city budget and tax rate adopted
ed82aab2c197cf10.summary: The council adopted Eagle Mountain's budget for the 2025-26 fiscal year and set the property tax rate at the certified rate.
ed82aab2c197cf10.impact: This is the spending plan for the year ahead and the rate behind your city property tax bill. The certified rate is the state-calculated baseline, so the city did not raise taxes above it.

edb99e343e2d8c8e.headline: Bypass Road land sale put on hold
edb99e343e2d8c8e.summary: The council delayed a decision on selling up to 20.35 acres of city-owned land known as the Bypass Road.
edb99e343e2d8c8e.impact: The city keeps the 20.35 acres for now. Any sale would have to come back to the council before it could go through.

eeae61b2ad0e4c58.headline: Consent agenda approved
eeae61b2ad0e4c58.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together in one vote; the record of the motion does not list which items were included.
eeae61b2ad0e4c58.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents.

efbacf0276cd6a16.headline: Parks and trails master plan sent back for changes
efbacf0276cd6a16.summary: The council delayed adopting the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan and sent it back to the consultant for revisions before a future work session.
efbacf0276cd6a16.impact: No park or trail is affected yet. The plan meant to guide future park and trail decisions is still being reworked and returns to the council later.

f000adff3dc5edb3.headline: Inland port decision put on hold
f000adff3dc5edb3.summary: The council delayed a decision on backing a Utah Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain, sending it back for more discussion.
f000adff3dc5edb3.impact: Nothing changes yet. The proposal is still alive and will come back to a future meeting, so if an inland port district in the city matters to you, there is still time to weigh in.

f10518dcbb90547f.headline: Brent Strong joins the planning commission
f10518dcbb90547f.summary: The council signed off on appointing Brent Strong to the planning commission for a three-year term running January 2026 through December 2028.
f10518dcbb90547f.impact: Nothing changes for you day to day. The planning commission reviews building and zoning proposals before they reach the council, so who sits on it shapes what gets built.

f2143c224ba5b9b3.headline: Mid-year changes to the city budget
f2143c224ba5b9b3.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the 2025-2026 city budget, the mid-year rewrite of what the city plans to spend.
f2143c224ba5b9b3.impact: Budget amendments move or add money partway through the year. This motion does not say which line items changed, so the detail lives in the budget document rather than the vote itself.

f22cc91c54e549db.headline: Consent agenda approved
f22cc91c54e549db.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items voted through together without separate discussion.
f22cc91c54e549db.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is routine housekeeping, and the record of the motion does not list which items were in the batch.

f31f4cd41d8c1c77.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled
f31f4cd41d8c1c77.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, holding item 12.C for a future meeting and adding an annual review to item 12.E.
f31f4cd41d8c1c77.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the routine batch approval of uncontested items, with one held back for another day.

f46007953488584e.headline: Lacie Messerly named city recorder
f46007953488584e.summary: The council appointed Lacie Messerly as Eagle Mountain's city recorder.
f46007953488584e.impact: Nothing changes for residents — the recorder is the staff position that keeps the city's official records and meeting minutes.

f51421a986885893.headline: Change to residential zoning rules rejected
f51421a986885893.summary: The council rejected proposed changes to the city's definitions and residential zoning rules, so those sections of the code stay as they are.
f51421a986885893.impact: Nothing changes for homeowners or builders — the existing residential zoning rules remain in force. The motion doesn't say what the rejected changes would have done.

f63342b5e7e2ce67.headline: Historic zones rules delayed again
f63342b5e7e2ce67.summary: The council put off a decision on new Historic Zone rules for a second time, pushing it to the August 6, 2024 meeting.
f63342b5e7e2ce67.impact: Nothing changes yet. If you own one of the older properties the city wants to bring under 2024 development rules, the decision is still pending.

f6a4a26cf9804ad4.headline: Tentative 2024-25 budget adopted, hearing June 4
f6a4a26cf9804ad4.summary: The council tentatively adopted the city's 2024-2025 budget and set a June 4, 2024 public hearing before the final budget is adopted.
f6a4a26cf9804ad4.impact: The June 4 hearing is your chance to speak on next year's city spending before the council locks it in.

f7618e5e6217129c.headline: Eagle Crest Storage facility approved
f7618e5e6217129c.summary: The city signed off on the site plan for Eagle Crest Storage, clearing the way for the storage facility to be built.
f7618e5e6217129c.impact: People living near the site will see a storage facility go up. The motion doesn't say exactly where it sits or how large it is.

f8c69fd69739e785.headline: Consent agenda approved
f8c69fd69739e785.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together in a single vote without separate discussion.
f8c69fd69739e785.impact: Nothing changes for residents on its own — consent items are the routine business the council clears all at once.

f922ac59e1387b98.headline: Noise and nuisance rules sent back to staff
f922ac59e1387b98.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's nuisance and noise rules, sending them to staff for revisions before the next meeting.
f922ac59e1387b98.impact: Nothing changes yet. If you've been following the city's noise or nuisance rules, the revised version is due back at the next council meeting.

f92496c7fbe3b1c2.headline: No decision on city facilities master plan
f92496c7fbe3b1c2.summary: The council did not adopt a Facilities Master Plan; a proposal to treat the Galloway report as a guideline for a future plan went no further.
f92496c7fbe3b1c2.impact: The city still has no adopted long-range plan for its buildings and facilities. Nothing changes for residents right now.

f9e4bc6085db8fdb.headline: Rod Hess appointed to the Planning Commission
f9e4bc6085db8fdb.summary: Rod Hess was appointed to the Planning Commission for a three-year term running through December 2026.
f9e4bc6085db8fdb.impact: Routine appointment, but worth knowing: the Planning Commission is the body that reviews development and zoning proposals before they reach the council.

fa21fe9624eac176.headline: Affordable housing plan put off
fa21fe9624eac176.summary: The council delayed adopting the city's affordable housing plan, sending it back for the changes members discussed before it returns at a future meeting.
fa21fe9624eac176.impact: Nothing changes for now. The plan is the city's road map for housing people can afford, and it comes back to the council at a later meeting.

faaef005a15d917b.headline: Noise limits now lift at 7 a.m. instead of 9 a.m.
faaef005a15d917b.summary: The city changed its noise rules, adjusting maximum decibel levels during restricted hours and moving the morning cutoff from 9 a.m. to 7 a.m., seven days a week.
faaef005a15d917b.impact: This applies citywide, weekends included: the stricter noise limits now end at 7 a.m. rather than 9 a.m., so you may hear louder activity two hours earlier in the morning.

faf564d49fb2618d.headline: Consent agenda approved, three items pulled
faf564d49fb2618d.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling three items out of the bundle for separate discussion later in the meeting.
faf564d49fb2618d.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the batch of routine items the council passes in a single vote, with the three pulled items taken up on their own.

fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.headline: Jessie Southworth joins Community Services Board
fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.summary: The council appointed Jessie Southworth to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, from April 2026 through March 2029.
fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is a volunteer appointment to an advisory board.

fbc813f79adcfb5f.headline: Firefly tank change order put on hold
fbc813f79adcfb5f.summary: The council delayed a decision on the second change order for the Firefly 4MG tank project.
fbc813f79adcfb5f.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now — the item comes back to the council at a later meeting.

fe9f6b250ca5fcce.headline: Enyo battery site rezoned back to agriculture
fe9f6b250ca5fcce.summary: The city rezoned the land known as the Enyo battery property from the airpark zone to the agriculture zone.
fe9f6b250ca5fcce.impact: The site is now farm-zoned rather than airpark-zoned, which narrows what can be built there. Nothing changes for residents day to day.

ff157f1cb6f92b8b.headline: Eagle Square commercial plat delayed
ff157f1cb6f92b8b.summary: The council delayed a decision on the preliminary plat for the Eagle Square commercial development.
ff157f1cb6f92b8b.impact: Nothing changes yet — the layout for this commercial project comes back to the council at a later meeting.

ffb8d6cc826597a7.headline: City budget amended for 2024-25
ffb8d6cc826597a7.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's 2024-2025 annual budget; the motion does not say which line items changed.
ffb8d6cc826597a7.impact: Budget amendments redirect real money mid-year. The motion itself names no amounts or projects, so the budget document is where to look for what actually shifted.
